[tal-a28-v01] Thus the obligatory rite has been declared; now the occasional rite is stated.

[tal-a28-v10] There we speak of the occasion rite: it is twofold, kula and akula; the first was declared in the glorious yoga course.

[tal-a28-v02] When the fixed future obligatory rite is established, primacy and identification follow; therefore all is occasional.

[tal-a28-v03] But in necessity arising from day and related conceptions, universal obligatoriness is stated from the necessity of days, months, stars, and years.

[tal-a28-v04] The wise call this occasional: sometimes arising, knower-determined existence.

[tal-a28-v05] Twilight worship, occasion worship, and this thread offering are always obligatory because of their fixed form for all under scripture.

[tal-a28-v06] Knowledge, scripture, teacher, brother, and group attainments, birth rite differences, and own birth festival association are listed.

[tal-a28-v07] Ancestral offering, calamity remedy, joy and wonder sight, yogini assembly, and meetings with own part and lineage are enumerated.

[tal-a28-v08] Scripture explanation, city residence, endings, ordered emergence, deity vision, dream command, and vow expiation are listed.

[tal-a28-v09] Thus occasional rites are determined in the glorious tantra essence in twenty-three divisions as the foundation of special worship.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v11] Ocean moon and sage are thus for maheśi; first and fifteenth belong to brahma lineage, and two to kaumari.

[tal-a28-v12] Ocean protector moon belongs to vaiṣṇavi; thirteenth to aindri; two to vārāhi; and a pair to caṇḍi.

[tal-a28-v13] Two lunar days belong to all; the tenth belongs to yogeśi, and the eighth also belongs to her, so it is proclaimed as two days.

[tal-a28-v14] Other akula occasions are marked in reverse; we speak of them as kula occasion as stated in bhairava kula.

[tal-a28-v15] In haiḍara, in trika existence and trika kali kula etc., this breath-supported time was first declared in detail.

[tal-a28-v16] That produces some own consciousness in wheel-difference movement; the time of gaining fullness of own consciousness is called occasion.

[tal-a28-v17] Occasion means filling; or the word occasion has etymology from the root meaning filling, from that filling.

[tal-a28-v18] Here in haiḍara the word is heard twofold; those skilled in that wheel movement have full consciousness.

[tal-a28-v19] Those joined in that assembly are devoted to that worship always; even one not identified worships at that time through own ordered worship.

[tal-a28-v20] From that yogini and siddha assembly one becomes identified, as in a spectacle seer consciousness becomes nondifferent.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v21] One immediately obtains ordered-risen full own consciousness by entering that, gained by yoga practice order.

[tal-a28-v22] They obtain immediately from entering consciousness unity; at that time consciousness is full and wish-milking.

[tal-a28-v23] By that, various fruit is obtained there at that time by worship quickly, as one with long-held wealth makes festival eagerly.

[tal-a28-v24] He favors a guest who arrived knowing that time; thus yogini and siddha leaders act for good fruit accomplishment.

[tal-a28-v25] Even diligent beings favor someone who recognizes the right time. Since this has already been explained, that general rule is enough here for the kula tradition.

[tal-a28-v26] O goddess, whichever mantra, yoga, or ritual sequence abides in someone's heart by the teacher's command becomes a source of accomplishment when it is carried out through worship.

[tal-a28-v27] O goddess, worship should be done according to kula conduct for the sake of accomplishment and liberation, and on fulfilment times the satiation offering is especially important.

[tal-a28-v28] O fair-faced goddess, those who negligently fail to make satiation offerings to the teachers and deities are badly behaved, corrupt, and no better than bound beings.

[tal-a28-v29] If daily worship has been missed, one must still worship on these fulfilment times. The wandering practice taught for gaining knowledge, power, and similar benefits is also connected with this.

[tal-a28-v30] The shakti sacrifice that has been taught, including rites of subjugation, attraction, and slaying, all succeed with ease on fulfilment days.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kramoditāṃ sadya eva labhate tatpraveśanāt / yogābhyāsakramopāttāṃ tathā pūrṇāṃ svasaṃvidam labhante sadya evaitatsaṃvidaikyapraveśanāt / tatkālaṃ cāpi saṃvitteḥ pūrṇatvāt kāmadogdhṛtā tena tattatphalaṃ tatra kāle saṃpūjayācirāt / yathā ciropāttadhanaḥ kurvannutsavamādarāt atithiṃ so@nugṛhṇāti tatkālābhijñamāgatam / tathā suphalasaṃsiddhyai yoginīsiddhanāyakāḥ yatnavanto@pi tatkālābhijñaṃ tamanugṛhṇate / uktaṃ ca tatra teneha kule sāmānyatetyalam yasya yaddhṛdaye devi vartate daiśikājñayā / mantro yogaḥ kramaścaiva pūjanāt siddhido bhavet kulācāreṇa deveśi pūjyaṃ siddhivimuktaye / ye parvasveṣu deveśi tarpaṇaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ gurūṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca na kurvanti pramādataḥ / durācārā hi te duṣṭāḥ paśutulyā varānane abhāvānnityapūjāyā avaśyaṃ hyeṣu pūjayet / aṭanaṃ jñānaśaktyādilābhārthaṃ yatprakīrtitam śaktiyāgaśca yaḥ prokto vaśyākarṣaṇamāraṇam / tatsarvaṃ parvadivaseṣvayatnenaiva siddhyati

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v31] The fulfilment time is defined in six ways, by general and special forms. Among these, the first and fifth days of the month are called auspicious days.

[tal-a28-v32] Because of its excellence, a fulfilment day is spoken of with the prefix 'śrī'. Since this appointed time is secret, it should not be named without that proper prefix.

[tal-a28-v33] In both lunar fortnights, the fourth, eighth, and final days are declared the most general fulfilment times.

[tal-a28-v34] If, on those same general fulfilment days, a future conjunction involving a planet and lunar mansion occurs, that twofold factor makes the day a general-special case.

[tal-a28-v35] Shambhu taught that this classification becomes elevenfold in each case, and among cases of the same kind the excellent one is to be distinguished.

[tal-a28-v36] This verse gives a coded list of fortnight and planetary combinations used in the fulfilment-time scheme, pairing lunar markers with sequences of planets and luminaries.

[tal-a28-v37] This verse lists the lunar mansions relevant to the schedule, including Phalguni, Tishya, Shravana, Shatabhisha, Mula, Prajapati, and Vishakha.

[tal-a28-v38] This verse sets out coded calendrical markers together with specific times such as first night, midnight, daybreak, and midday for the ritual schedule.

[tal-a28-v39] At the appointed time called first night, in the months beginning with Margashirsha, the female messenger may be a maiden, a woman of low birth, or a courtesan, provided she is passionate and knows reality.

[tal-a28-v40] In expanded or condensed form and in proper order, worship should be done in the circle called the after-sacrifice. On fulfilment days this after-sacrifice circle should be performed with special emphasis.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatsāmānyaviśeṣābhyāṃ ṣoḍhā parva nirūpitam / māsasyādyaṃ pañcamaṃ ca śrīdinaṃ paribhāṣyate utkṛṣṭatvāt parvadinaṃ śrīpūrvatvena bhāṣyate / samayo hyeṣa yadguptaṃ tannānupapadaṃ vadet turyāṣṭamānyabhuvanacaramāṇi dvayorapi / pakṣayoriha sāmānyasāmānyaṃ parva kīrtitam yadeteṣu dineṣveva bhaviṣyadgrahabhātmakaḥ / ubhayātmā viśeṣaḥ syāttatsāmānyaviśeṣatā sā caikādaśadhaikasminnekasminvibhunoditā / sajātīyā tu sotkṛṣṭetyevaṃ śambhurnyarūpayat kṛṣṇayugaṃ vahnisitaṃ śrutikṛṣṇaṃ vahnisitamiti pakṣāḥ / arkendujīvacandrā budhayugmendvarkakaviguruvidhu syāt paraphalguścaitramaghe tiṣyaḥ prākphalgukarṇaśatabhiṣajaḥ / mūlaprājāpatye viśākhikā śravaṇasaṃjñayā bhāni randhre tithyarkapare vasurandhre śaśivṛṣāṅkarasarandhrayugam / prathamaniśāmadhyaniśe madhyāhnaśarā dinodayo madhyadinam prathamaniśeti ca samayo mārgaśiraḥprabhṛtimāseṣu / kanyāntyajātha veśyā rāgavatī tattvavedinī dūtī vyāsasamāsāt kramaśaḥ pūjyāścakre@nuyāgākhye / sarvatra ca parvadine kuryādanuyāgacakramatiśayataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v41] When the after-sacrifice is carried out completely, following the sequence of hidden and open rules and the conduct of the initial sacrifice, it is indeed foremost in every ritual application.

[tal-a28-v42] When the proper time for the after-sacrifice is available, one should make every effort to use it. But in the month of Ashvayuj there is no such special lunar-mansion and planetary time, so that month is excluded.

[tal-a28-v43] The reckoning of time, lunar mansion, and planet has been explained for eleven months. In Phalguna, the twelfth day of the bright fortnight is declared as a special fulfilment time.

[tal-a28-v44] Here the foremost special factor is the conjunction involving the piercing of the prior lunar day. Day and night are divided into three parts, giving a first, middle, and last division.

[tal-a28-v45] Within that threefold division, the best time for worship is when the foremost time-slot coincides with the right lunar mansion and planet, and the ritual circle aligns with them.

[tal-a28-v46] On fulfilment times, the initial sacrifice and desire-driven rites can succeed through worship alone, provided the day, time-slot, lunar mansion, and planet are properly arranged and their gentle or fierce nature is taken into account.

[tal-a28-v47] Having understood the nature of the timing, the foremost practitioner should perform the appropriate task. But what if the lunar mansion, planet, and lunar day fall outside the declared time for worship?

[tal-a28-v48] Some say that if there is a conflict, one should ignore the special astrological factor and follow the conventional worship time. But our teachers disagree: here the lunar day is the decisive special factor, not the mere time-slot.

[tal-a28-v49] The lunar day becomes fully clear through the moon portion and the clusters of sun-rays, measured by planets and stars.

[tal-a28-v50] Therefore the lunar day is primary here, qualified by union of planets and stars, while time is not principal; thus speaks the supreme lord.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-guptāguptavidhānādiyāgacaryākrameṇa sampūrṇam / anuyāgaḥ kila mukhyaḥ sarvasminneva karmaviniyoge anuyāgakālalābhe tasmātprayateta tatparamaḥ / bhagrahasamayaviśeṣo nāśvayuje ko@pi tena tadvarjam velābhagrahakalanā kathitaikādaśasu māseṣu / phālgunamāse śuklaṃ yatproktaṃ dvādaśīdinaṃ parva agratithivedhayogo mukhyatamo@sau viśeṣo@tra / divasaniśe kila kṛtvā tribhāgaśaḥ prathamamadhyamāparavibhāgaḥ pūjākālastatra tribhāgite mukhyatamaḥ kālaḥ / yadi saṃghaṭeta velā mukhyatamā bhagrahau tathā cakram tadyāga ādiyāgastatkāmyaṃ pūjayaiva parvasu siddhyet / dinavelābhagrahakalpanena tatrāpi saumyaraudratvam jñātvā sādhakamukhyastattatkāryaṃ tadā tadā kuryāt / ukto yo@rcākālastaṃ cedullaṅghya bhagrahatithiḥ syāt tamanādṛtya viśeṣaṃ pradhānayetsāmayamiti kecit / neti tvasmadguravo viśeṣarūpā hi tithiriha na velā saṃvedyarūpaśaśadharabhāgaḥ saṃvedakārkakaranikaraiḥ / yāvānyāvati pūrṇaḥ sā hi tithirbhagrahaiḥ sphuṭībhavati tasmānmukhyātra tithiḥ sā ca viśeṣyā graharkṣayogena / velātra na pradhānaṃ yuktaṃ caitattathāhi parameśaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v51] In the Trika Bhairava Kula scriptures it is said that on festival days no time-union is accepted; another arises from lunar-day, star, and planet union.

[tal-a28-v52] The lunar day is worshipful because of its principal form; in the absence of white, they say black goat sacrifice indeed.

[tal-a28-v53] What scripture states again about waves and so forth: even time-stated desired rule is indicated by primacy; and there, on the Pausha festival day.

[tal-a28-v54] Having worshipped, meditated, and chanted at midnight, the command bears fruit for one who has gone outside; so in Magha, speech from the circle bears fruit.

[tal-a28-v55] Soon comes desired accomplishment: in five there is friendship, wealth, and union; in the circle place, enemy destruction arises from anger and stone splitting.

[tal-a28-v56] Attainment of accomplished command to the path's end is said by the lord; in absence of star-planet union, time is considered, but the lunar day must necessarily be observed.

[tal-a28-v57] That clear form indeed, of the lunar day's natural rise, would give following star, planet, lunar day, and time parts; but the day is all-limb beautiful.

[tal-a28-v58] If it could be obtained, then most special worship should be arranged in this; and not only desired, only this in avoidance, because it is said.

[tal-a28-v59] Break of convention: in the glorious Bhairava Kula wave scripture, corrupt, bad-conducted, animal-like indeed are those who do not know the festival.

[tal-a28-v60] Non-performance of the desired rite would never be sinful; there, for accomplishment of follow-up sacrifice, circle-sacrifice is determined.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śrītrikabhairavakulaśāstreṣūce na parvadivaseṣu / velāyogaṃ kaṃcana tithibhagrahayogato hyanyam tithistu pūjyā pradhānarūpatvāt / śvetābhāve kṛṣṇacchāgālambhaṃ hi kathayanti yatpunarūrmiprabhṛtini śāstre veloditāpi tatkāmyam / mukhyatayoddiśya vidhiṃ tathāca tatra pauṣaparvadine kṛtvārcanamardhaniśi dhyātvā japtvā bahirgatasya yathā / ādeśaḥ phalati tathā māghe cakrādvacaḥ phalati acirādabhīṣṭasiddhiḥ pañcasu maitrī dhanaṃ ca melāpaḥ / cakrasthāne krodhāt pāṣāṇasphoṭanena ripunāśaḥ siddhādeśaprāptirmārgāntaṃ kathyate vibhunā / bhagrahayogābhāve velāṃ tu titheravaśyamīkṣeta sā hi tathā sphuṭarūpā titheḥ svabhāvodayaṃ dadyāt / bhagrahatithivelāṃśānuyāyi sarvāṅgasundaraṃ tu dinam yadi labhyeta tadāsminviśeṣatamapūjanaṃ racayet / naca kāmyameva kevalametatparivarjane yataḥ kathitaḥ samayavilopaḥ śrīmadbhairavakula ūrmiśāstre ca / duṣṭā hi durācārāḥ paśutulyāḥ parva ye na viduḥ naca kāmyasyākaraṇe syājjātu pratyavāyitvam / tatrānuyāgasiddhyarthaṃ cakrayāgo nirūpyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v61] Image-sacrifice is thus called in the glorious Yogishvari doctrine: obligatory and occasional rite, which is said here by the great lord.

[tal-a28-v62] Circle-sacrifice is primary everywhere, especially in desired rites, for a knower, yogi, man, or woman in this image-named context.

[tal-a28-v63] In yoga, with effort, that should indeed be joined: the supreme vessel; from contact with that, fullness would be, in Traishirasa and so forth.

[tal-a28-v64] By that, all that is offered and done, the three worlds moving and still, is for the knower or yogi; whoever gives or does.

[tal-a28-v65] Even after initiation, declared food is Brahma, essence, Hari, consumer, Shiva; thus the knower uplifts even dog-cookers.

[tal-a28-v66] Having become composed of all principles, if he eats, he is a practitioner; by mere feeding, ten million are fed.

[tal-a28-v67] Then, dear one, if the knower of principles in this would eat, count would not be known; thus says blessed Shiva.

[tal-a28-v68] All food is Maya-composed; Shiva is consumer, and indeed I; who indeed knows thus is teacher and principle-crosser.

[tal-a28-v69] Having seen him, god coming, the playing herbs in the house say: turned back today by us from the dense ocean of samsara.

[tal-a28-v70] Having attained whose face, we shall go to the supreme state; others are drinkers; indeed upward, while prana and apana are downward-faced.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mūrtiyāga iti prokto yaḥ śrīyogīśvarīmate / nityaṃ naimittikaṃ karma yadatroktaṃ maheśinā sarvatra cakrayāgo@tra mukhyaḥ kāmye viśeṣataḥ / jñānī yogī ca puruṣaḥ strī vāsminmūrtisaṃjñake yoge prayatnato yojyastaddhi pātramanuttaram / tatsaṃparkātpūrṇatā syāditi traiśirasādiṣu tena sarvaṃ hutaṃ ceṣṭaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram / jñānine yogine vāpi yo dadāti karoti vā dīkṣottare@pi ca proktamannaṃ brahmā raso hariḥ / bhoktā śiva iti jñānī śvapacānapyathoddhareat sarvatattvamayo bhūtvā yadi bhuṅkte sa sādhakaḥ / tena bhojitamātreṇa sakṛtkoṭistu bhojitā atha tattvavidetasminyadi bhuñjīta tat priye / parisaṃkhyā na vidyeta tadāha bhagavāñchivaḥ bhojyaṃ māyātmakaṃ sarvaṃ śivo bhoktā sa cāpyaham / evaṃ yo vai vijānāti daiśikastattvapāragaḥ taṃ dṛṣṭvā devamāyāntaṃ krīḍantyoṣadhayo gṛhe / nivṛttamadyaivāsmābhiḥ saṃsāragahanārṇavāt yadasya vaktraṃ saṃprāptā yāsyāmaḥ paramaṃ padam / anye@pānabhujo hyūrdhve prāṇo@pānastvadhomukhaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v71] In that consumer, O goddess, even hundreds of families of the giver are quickly released from the ocean of hell-torture.

[tal-a28-v72] In the glorious Nishatana it is also said: even from seeking narration, having reached inside the ear, having gone out from the teacher's mouth.

[tal-a28-v73] Even a drinker of liquor, a thief, a killer of a brahmin, or one who violates the teacher's bed is freed at the very moment of death; only the body remains.

[tal-a28-v74] Whether last-born or twice-born, child, old, or young, even a border-dweller who is a knower becomes a purifier of the land.

[tal-a28-v75] There the god is present with the goddess and attendants; therefore, one should first honor the teacher who is skilled in knowledge.

[tal-a28-v76] One should perform the worship of his form; according to the Yogīśvarīmata, this is done during the thread offering, at śrāddha, and fully on festival days.

[tal-a28-v77] It should also be done at solar and lunar eclipses, at worldly festivals and celebrations, at marriages and the like, and during the sacrificial rites of brahmins.

[tal-a28-v78] The form-worship should be performed at initiation, consecration, purification of observances, and for the sake of a desired aim; it is of five kinds.

[tal-a28-v79] The five types are the single, the paired, the mixed, the circle-joined, and the hero-mingled. The single is done by teachers alone, and the mixed is done by teachers together with others.

[tal-a28-v80] The paired worship is done with practitioners and others together with their wives; it is of two kinds, either through union with one's wife or through union with a courtesan who has been brought by payment.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tasminbhoktari deveśi dātuḥ kulaśatānyapi / āśveva parimucyante narakādyātanārṇavāt śrīmanniśāṭane@pyuktaṃ kathanānveṣaṇādapi / śrotrābhyantarasaṃprāpte guruvaktrādvinirgate muktastadaiva kāle tu yantraṃ tiṣṭhati kevalam / surāpaḥ steyahārī ca brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ antyajo vā dvijo vātha bālo vṛddho yuvāpi vā / paryantavāsī yo jñānī deśasyāpi pavitrakaḥ tatra saṃnihito devaḥ sadevīkaḥ sakiṅkaraḥ / tasmātprādhānyataḥ kṛtvā guruṃ jñānaviśāradam mūrtiyāgaṃ carettasya vidhiryogīśvarīmate / pavitrārohaṇe śrāddhe tathā parvadineṣvalam sūryacandroparāgādau laukikeṣvapi parvasu / utsave ca vivāhādau viprāṇāṃ yajñakarmaṇi dīkṣāyāṃ ca pratiṣṭhāyāṃ samayānāṃ viśodhane / kāmanārthaṃ ca kartavyo mūrtiyāgaḥ sa pañcadhā kevalo yāmalo miśraścakrayugvīrasaṅkaraḥ / kevalaḥ kevalaireva gurubhirmiśritaḥ punaḥ sādhakādyaiḥ sapatnīkairyāmalaḥ sa dvidhā punaḥ / patnīyogāt krayānītaveśyāsaṃyogato@thavā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v81] The circle-women and other fitting partners in power-union will be explained later; worship joined with them becomes the circle-joined rite, which grants all fruits.

[tal-a28-v82] The worship performed together with all is called the hero-mingled rite; the teacher should be in the center, and the group of teachers forms the surrounding circle.

[tal-a28-v83] Outside there are three enclosures in due order, extending up to the pledged initiates; or all may be arranged in rows, but in every case the teacher is always in the middle.

[tal-a28-v84] Then, following the order of the circle, one should worship with his scent, incense, garland, touch, and garment, recognizing, 'This is that very circle.'

[tal-a28-v85] In a one-spoked circle one should contemplate the single-hero rite; in a two-spoked circle the paired rite; and in others, such as a six-spoked circle, the triad and so forth.

[tal-a28-v86] One should place six yoginīs in a sixfold form, a group of seven in a seven-spoked circle, octads in an eightfold form, or any other such group in a circle of corresponding shape.

[tal-a28-v87] Then the wise one should first worship the circle in a vessel filled with liquid, placed on a support; satiation should never be done without a support.

[tal-a28-v88] Without a support there is a lapse, the radiant powers are not pleased, and the vessel becomes like a ghost, even if it holds śākta nectar and liquor.

[tal-a28-v89] There the power is the enjoyer, and that same reality is Śambhu, the supreme lord; thus one should meditate on the united triad of the individual, power, and Śiva.

[tal-a28-v90] Then the satiation should be performed for each enclosure in order; by the method of reabsorption, one should then lead it back within.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v100] A wise person should not give a ritual fee smaller than half a rūpaka; for the initiates it should increase in order, doubled step by step, up to the guru.

[tal-a28-v91] When the movement reaches the teacher, that is called the full circulation; in it, the deities are satisfied first and then the heroes. Such is the order.

[tal-a28-v92] According to our teacher's order, the hero and the hero-power are honored thus; then various portions of food, together with meat, fish, and the like, are offered.

[tal-a28-v93] There the best practitioner should scatter the offerings in front until complete satisfaction; if no vessel is available, he should use the bhadra or the rolled shell.

[tal-a28-v94] According to the Siddhāmata, the wise one should make a vessel with the hands: the bhadra is formed with the right hand, and the other is called the rolled shell.

[tal-a28-v95] One should place the little finger of the right hand upon the left, join the forefinger and thumb, and place the fingers of the left hand below the right.

[tal-a28-v96] When the two hands are bound without any gap, that is called the rolled shell; but if, at the time of drinking, drops fall to the ground, the gesture has not been properly formed.

[tal-a28-v97] By that stream the rays please Vetala, Guhyaka, and the other deities, and Bhairava too is pleased; therefore drinking from the hand is the supreme practice.

[tal-a28-v98] No one should be given entry to this rite in advance; but if someone enters by carelessness, one should not conduct any inquiry about that person.

[tal-a28-v99] Having performed the rite in this way, the wise person should, at its conclusion and in due order, distribute the ritual fee together with respectful touch, betel, cloth, and other such gifts.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v101] This is the mūrti-yāga, the foremost of all worships; but in a rite performed for a specific desire, it should be done seven times in the same way.

[tal-a28-v102] First the Mothers recognize the house, then they perceive its capability and its strength or weakness, and afterward the Mothers are filled with amazement.

[tal-a28-v103] Then they draw near, are pleased, and grant boons; and the goddesses and the Lord, together with their retinues, are fully present.

[tal-a28-v104] Therefore this beloved mūrti-yāga should be performed by the wise in a pleasing, hidden house, with the heroes and the śaktis fully joined together.

[tal-a28-v105] Participants may be brought in without prior arrangement through the recitation of deity names; but if the mūrti circle cannot be obtained, one should worship only maidens.

[tal-a28-v106] For a desire-rite, one must not choose a maiden who is bodily impaired or menstruating; the rite is also tied to the first lunar day with Śravaṇa and the fourth day with the three Uttara stars.

[tal-a28-v107] The fifth day is with Hasta; the sixth with the Pūrva stars and Punarvasu; the seventh and the next with Maghā; and likewise the ninth with Rohiṇī.

[tal-a28-v108] The twelfth day is with Mūla, the fourteenth with Aśvinī, the full moon is included, and the new moon is with Dhaniṣṭhā; this forms an elevenfold set.

[tal-a28-v109] A day joined with Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, or Friday, or another suitable day, is well known as a yoga-parvan, whether it occurs by night or by day.

[tal-a28-v110] The mūrti-yāga should certainly be performed on a yoga-parvan; the wise person should honor all days called yoga-parvans with the mūrti-yāga.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v111] Through the mūrti-yāga, even without the mandala rite, a person can become a vow-holder; thus is the mūrti-yāga taught in the revered Siddhayogīśvarīmata.

[tal-a28-v112] Now the clear pavitraka rite taught by Śiva is explained, as it has been indicated in the revered Ratnamālā and Triśiras scriptures.

[tal-a28-v113] Among the teachings of the Siddha, Āṭana, Sadbhāva, Mālinī, and Sāra traditions, the procedure taught principally in the revered Mālā is now explained.

[tal-a28-v114] The serpent king, stupefied by a poison-born sleep from the churning of the milk ocean, could not remain in his own realm during the rainy season.

[tal-a28-v115] Pure and living only on air, he worshipped Lord Bhairava thoroughly for a hundred divine years, a span multiplied tenfold.

[tal-a28-v116] He appealed to the pleased Lord, saying that during the rains he was unable to remain in his own netherworld; and the Supreme Lord responded to him.

[tal-a28-v117] The Supreme Lord placed the serpent king upon the seat of his own matted locks; then all the hosts of gods bore him upon their heads.

[tal-a28-v118] For the great and honored, universal reverence is no wonder; therefore the serpent king came to rest on the head of the Great Lord and, in every way, on the gods as well.

[tal-a28-v119] One should prepare that pavitra for oneself, preceded by worship; even ten crores of acts of worship are not equal to the pavitra offering.

[tal-a28-v120] Without the pavitra and related rites, initiation is in vain, knowledge is in vain, and even worship of the guru is in vain; by Śiva's command, the serpent would take their fruit away.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v121] Therefore, with all effort, that rite should be done by knowers of kula when the sun stands in the Gemini-Cancer position.

[tal-a28-v122] It should be performed with restraint until that Libra full moon; the last day of Kartika is also held as the term.

[tal-a28-v123] Other readers, knowers of eternal tantra, make a different explanation and take the last dark day of Kartika.

[tal-a28-v124] The fullness of the eternal kula wheel is, in one opinion, on the last bright day of Magha, called kula parvan.

[tal-a28-v125] There the fullness belongs to the moon; that lunar day is the kula full moon, and the south-north moving time is declared kula or akula.

[tal-a28-v126] Fullness is said on the last day of that kula, because of the duty in the southern half-year in the rite.

[tal-a28-v127] In the thread offering, for accomplishment of manifestation, the god manifested that form described in many scriptures concerning the dark path.

[tal-a28-v128] By one word alone in the Sri Ratnamala kula agama, at that time, it is complete of all rites.

[tal-a28-v129] The thread offering rite should be done in the bright fortnight in every way, with filling by shakti union, shakti-self, and white petal.

[tal-a28-v130] From affinity with the southern half-year, therefore that rite is called by the one-to-six lata one, the great.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v131] Make a gold-jewel-marked knot; make a pearl thread offering with threefold gold thread and one hundred knots for the teacher.

[tal-a28-v132] For another teacher, it is three more than the middle ocean; for the supreme lord, previously accomplished teacher yoga lord; in that domain, more than essence.

[tal-a28-v133] Eight more is said for Shiva, filled with various gems; in vidya pitha bead thread beginning, like teacher, like Shiva, again.

[tal-a28-v134] For vaṭuka, in absence of gold, silver should be arranged; then cotton thread, linen, cotton, three-times-twisted.

[tal-a28-v135] From ninefold thread, threefold onward, make up to a sun-ray multiple; even from that, threefold or.

[tal-a28-v136] From that, eighteen-thread is lowest; middle is again one hundred eight; from that, threefold is highest, held opinion.

[tal-a28-v137] Knots counted by principles, from six-path calculation or by expansion and contraction, are variegated and filled with good scent.

[tal-a28-v138] By special rite, first worship, then offer the thread offering, from meditation on the complete all-paths.

[tal-a28-v139] From knee to crown of guru and self, or; then a great festival is to be done, preceded by teacher worship.

[tal-a28-v140] All scripture followers are to be satisfied with gifts, clothes, and food; the great festival is performed, consisting of song and dance.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v141] The period is four months, seven days, or three days from non-attainment; at its end, appease the god and dismiss mandala and so forth.

[tal-a28-v142] Fire and afterward circle sacrifice are to be done as previously stated: in month, in month, in four months, in year, or even thread offering.

[tal-a28-v143] In every way it is to be performed according to means; in absence of wealth, again to be done even with kusha bound.

[tal-a28-v144] When wealth is present, again deceit leads to disease and hell; in daily worships, fullness comes from festival worship completion.

[tal-a28-v145] Even there, fullness comes from thread worship; but if the thread is lost, the wise one should chant expiation.

[tal-a28-v146] Being well purified, one should act again according to the supreme lord's command; now the clear rite for the three-headed form is declared and written.

[tal-a28-v147] Here is said the Shaiva three-measure system, five-five-natured, with ten and eighteen distinctions, of six streams.

[tal-a28-v148] Those men who have fallen from vow, corrupt teacher and scriptures, and lack obligatory and occasional ritual joints.

[tal-a28-v149] Whether from unwillingness or willingness, those committing subtle sins have the thread made for their pacification in Shiva.

[tal-a28-v150] From the start of Shravana to the end of Kartika, in the bright fortnight that gives auspiciousness, not in the dark fortnight that gives sorrow, among doers, realms, kings and others.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v151] Cotton thread, silk, cotton, and linen indeed are for the four stages; they are cut and washed by the fair-browed one.

[tal-a28-v152] In three ways, having tripled the mental count, one should make one hundred eight threads, or half of that, or a quarter of that.

[tal-a28-v153] The decrease is from the previous count, by tens in order, by nines, by fives, or by twenty-seven, from Shiva onward.

[tal-a28-v154] Whatever the thread arrangement, one should make that many knots, or four evenly smeared with saffron.

[tal-a28-v155] In the manifest linga it should end at the seat, in images it is beautiful on the head, from arrangement of three principles.

[tal-a28-v156] The twelve-knot powers and Brahma-face rays are in the knowledge seat, moving linga, altar, and teacher group.

[tal-a28-v157] In bell, ladle and spoon, disciple linga-bearers, gate arch, own body, and fire seat, it is desired as beautiful.

[tal-a28-v158] In temple and sacrifice house one should make the nine-colored; in the knowledge seat, sixteen arrows go to image, linga, and seat.

[tal-a28-v159] Eight Vedas in the bell, eighteen arrow-eyes in the spoon, thirty-six Veda-eyes in the ladle, sun in temple and pavilion.

[tal-a28-v160] Mercury-moon; in bath house eye and meditation house; in teacher seven accomplishers go, in son five, in vow seven.
