chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v161] Four in other scripture, five is said in disciple; for linga-bearers only, ten knots should be arranged in the arch.

[tal-a28-v162] Eight knots should be in the gates; having done thus and worshipped the thread, the mantra net is placed there, then.

[tal-a28-v163] Having prepared the threads, one should do the confluence rite; then for a year one should meditate Bhairava, witness of holes.

[tal-a28-v164] Having given the full offering, O goddess, one should bow to mantra Bhairava; om, toward the lord who fills all rite faults, the vow.

[tal-a28-v165] Whatever unmade or corrupt made, O son of Mother, all that is mine, O lord of gods, may perish by your grace.

[tal-a28-v166] In every way, O lord of the ray wheel, salutation to you; be gracious to me; by this the invitation thread should be given to the god.

[tal-a28-v167] The teacher should then give offering to yogini field mothers: five-cow-products, oblation, and tooth-stick, by disciples all around.

[tal-a28-v168] The teacher should sleep; rising early, do the daily rite; then, having worshipped the rite, gather the threads.

[tal-a28-v169] Join tooth-stick, clay, nurse, prosperous nurse, water, and ash in the five places.

[tal-a28-v170] Place the five purifiers in order in the front, right, west, up, and left mouths within Shiva's range.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-catvāro@thānyaśāstrasthe śiṣye pañcakamucyate / liṅgināṃ kevalo granthistoraṇe daśa kalpayet dvāreṣvaṣṭau granthayaḥ syuḥ kṛtvetthaṃ tu pavitrakam / pūjayitvā mantrajālaṃ tatsthatvātmasthate tataḥ pavitrakāṇāṃ saṃpādya kuryātsaṃpātasaṃskriyām / tataḥ saṃvatsaraṃ dhyāyedbhairavaṃ chidrasākṣiṇam dattvā pūrṇāhutiṃ devi praṇamenmantrabhairavam / oṃ samastakriyādoṣapūraṇeśa vrataṃ prati yatkiṃcidakṛtaṃ duṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ vā mātṛnandana / tatsarvaṃ mama deveśa tvatprasādātpraṇaśyatu sarvathā raśmicakreśa namastubhyaṃ prasīda me / anena dadyāddevāya nimantraṇapavitrakam yoginīkṣetramātṝṇāṃ baliṃ dadyāttato guruḥ / pañcagavyaṃ caruṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ śiṣyaiḥ samantataḥ ācārya nidrāṃ kurvīta prātarutthāya cāhnikam / tato vidhiṃ pūjayitvā pavitrāṇi samāharet dantakāṣṭhaṃ mṛcca dhātrī samṛddhātrī sahāmbunā / catuḥsamaṃ ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ bhasma pañcasu yojayet prāgdakṣapaścimordhvasthavāmavaktreṣu vai kramāt / pañcaitāni pavitrāṇi sthāpayecceśagocare

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v171] Employ kusha fuel and the five cow products at Sharva's front; then offer the threefold food joined with left nectar.

[tal-a28-v172] Give blood, wine, and various drinks; then perform oblation with great-earth-born flesh mixed with sesame.

[tal-a28-v173] Alternatively use sesame with ghee, or rice with grains, along with sugar pieces soaked in the five nectars.

[tal-a28-v174] Cast the root mantra a thousand and eight times, the flames a hundred and eight times, then the full offering.

[tal-a28-v175] Taking the purifier in the palms, recite this to the lord: whatever was done by me from desire or unwillingness.

[tal-a28-v176] May that flawless state be mine, O lord, through the purifier and your command; may the root mantra fulfill the rite rule.

[tal-a28-v177] Give the purifier ending in vaushat, then in order three purifiers ending in nada, samana, and unmana.

[tal-a28-v178] The elemental practitioner gives the fourfold in direct order; the dedicated practitioner gives the fourfold purifier in reverse order.

[tal-a28-v179] Whatever various items such as clothes, umbrellas, ornaments, lamp garlands, and a gold sesame vessel are offered.

[tal-a28-v180] For complete fulfillment, Shiva devotees are to be fed and worshipped according to ability, with a pair of cloths.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kuśedhma pañcagavyaṃ ca śarvāgre viniyojayet / vāmāmṛtādisaṃyuktaṃ naivedyaṃ trividhaṃ tataḥ dadyādasṛk tathā madyaṃ pānāni vividhāni ca / tato homo mahākṣmājamāṃsaistilayutairatho tilairghṛtayutairyadvā taṇḍulairatha dhānyakaiḥ / śarkarākhaṇḍasaṃyuktapañcāmṛtapariplutaiḥ mūlaṃ sahasraṃ sāṣṭoktaṃ triśaktau brahmavaktrakam / arciṣāṃ tu śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ kṣipet tato@ñjalau pavitraṃ tu gṛhītvā prapaṭhedidam / akāmādathavā kāmādyanmayā na kṛtaṃ vibho tadacchidraṃ mamāstvīśa pavitreṇa tavājñayā / mūlamantraḥ pūrayeti kriyāniyamamityatha vauṣaḍantaṃ pavitraṃ ca dadyādbindvavasānakam / nādāntaṃ samanāntaṃ cāpyunmanāntaṃ kramāttrayam evaṃ catuṣṭayaṃ dadyādanulomena bhautikaḥ / naiṣṭhikastu vilomena pavitrakacatuṣṭayam yatkiñcidvividhaṃ vastracchatrālaṅkaraṇādikam / tannivedyaṃ dīpamālāḥ suvarṇatilabhājanam vastrayugmayutaṃ sarvasampūraṇanimittataḥ / bhojanīyāḥ pūjanīyāḥ śivabhaktāstu śaktitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v181] Perform the great festival for the specified month and day period; afterward they should never go to another place.

[tal-a28-v182] The teacher is to be worshipped and given a new milk-giving cow adorned with gold, jewels, silver, and cloth.

[tal-a28-v183] The guru should say, "Your rite is complete," to be said for the god of gods and for his return.

[tal-a28-v184] Then dismissal is done; the guru takes the hidden ornaments and food offering for sacrifice and employs them.

[tal-a28-v185] The common purifier of the four is remembered; no higher vow exists, and what praise of it is declared.

[tal-a28-v186] Do not cast the remainder into deep water flow; place it firmly. Then the occasional rite previously taught by me follows.

[tal-a28-v187] There, worship of the god is especially to be done, and the wheel sacrifice is to be performed by the wise according to the previously stated method.

[tal-a28-v188] There, whatever helps desired enjoyment or liberation, whether by tradition or directly, and whether of conscious or unconscious self, qualifies.

[tal-a28-v189] That is worshipful; its means are worshipful for attaining identity with it, and means such as image, time, and rite are fully worshipped.

[tal-a28-v190] Through its worship the means gains capacity; by becoming identical with its form, one quickly obtains the goal.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-catustridvyekamāsādidinaikāntaṃ mahotsavam / kuryāttato na vrajeyuranyasthānaṃ kadācana tatastu daiśikaḥ pūjyo gāmasmai kṣīriṇīṃ navām / dadyātsuvarṇaratnādirupyavastravibhūṣitām vadedguruśca saṃpūrṇo vidhistava bhavatviti / vaktavyaṃ devadevasya punarāgamanāya ca tato visarjanaṃ kāryaṃ guptamābharaṇādikam / naivedyaṃ gururādāya yāgārthe tanniyojayet caturṇāmapi sāmānyaṃ pavitrakamiti smṛtam / nāsmādvrataṃ paraṃ kiñcit kā vāsya stutirucyate śeṣaṃ tvagādhe vāryoghe kṣipenna sthāpayetsthiram / atha naimittikavidhiryaḥ purāsūtrito mayā sa bhaṇyate tatra kāryā devasyārcā viśeṣataḥ / cakrayāgaśca kartavyaḥ pūrvoktavidhinā budhaiḥ tatra yadyannijābhīṣṭabhogamokṣopakārakam / pāramparyeṇa sākṣādvā bhaveccidacidātmakam tatpūjyaṃ tadupāyāśca pūjyāstanmayatāptaye / tadupāyo@pi saṃpūjyo mūrtikālakriyādikaḥ upeyasūtisāmarthyamupāyatvaṃ tadarcanāt / tadrūpatanmayībhāvādupeyaṃ śīghramāpnuyāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v191] As there is non-proximity in the means, so inevitable task-ness follows, especially in worship and related rites.

[tal-a28-v192] When the acquisition of some knowledge that helps enjoyment and liberation is declared primary, the occasional day is declared primary by the wise.

[tal-a28-v193] The means to that knowledge is the scripture, and the teacher is a suitable speaker. Even a fellow disciple who knows that scripture can impart knowledge through dialogue.

[tal-a28-v194] The teacher's wife, brother, son, and others belong to this group not because of birth relations, but because of their connection with knowledge.

[tal-a28-v195] Those established in body and ego through the development of seed and blood form a lineage that supports the body, and this is fully established among blood relatives.

[tal-a28-v196] And so, in the traditional law texts, inheritance by lineage is indeed fitting, since it is determined by the distinction between nearer and more distant relations.

[tal-a28-v197] But those who have abandoned attachment to the body and share in awareness and the sense of I enjoy kinship through two lineages that support awareness.

[tal-a28-v198] In this regard, when one's seeing and acting are opened by the Lord's power, one understands that this body is indeed made from a series of earlier material causes.

[tal-a28-v199] The self is free from change and, being eternal, has no cause; yet by its own freedom it remains as if concealed.

[tal-a28-v200] And again, when it becomes manifest and attains the state of Bhairava, that manifestation is strongly characterized by both enjoyment and liberation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yathā yathā ca naikaṭyamupāyeṣu tathā tathā / avaśyaṃbhāvi kāryatvaṃ viśeṣāccārcanādike jñānasya kasyacitprāptirbhogamokṣopakāriṇaḥ / yadā tanmukhyamevoktaṃ naimittikadinaṃ budhaiḥ tadupāyaḥ śāstramatra vaktāpyaupayiko guruḥ / tadvidyo@pi gurubhrātā saṃvādājjñānadāyakaḥ guroḥ patnī tathā bhrātā putra ityādiko gaṇaḥ / na yonisaṃbandhavaśādvidyāsaṃbandhajastu saḥ vīryāruṇaparīṇāmadehāhantāpratiṣṭhitāḥ / dehopakārasantānā jñāteye pariniṣṭhitāḥ tathāca smṛtiśāstreṣu santaterdāyahāritā / yuktaiva tāvānsa hyukto bhedāddūrāntikatvataḥ ye tu tyaktaśarīrāsthā bodhāhambhāvabhāginaḥ / bodhopakārasantānadvayātte bandhutājuṣaḥ tatretthaṃ prāgyadā paśyecchaktyunmīlitadṛkkriyaḥ / dehastāvadayaṃ pūrvapūrvopādānanirmitaḥ ātmā vikārarahitaḥ śāśvatatvādahetukaḥ / svātantryāt punarātmīyādayaṃ channa iva sthitaḥ punaśca prakaṭībhūya bhairavībhāvabhājanam / tatrāsya prakaṭībhāve bhuktimuktyātmake bhṛśam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v201] The suitable means for this is the lineage of knowledge, operating through a stream of such and similar knowledge that gradually becomes clear.

[tal-a28-v202] As what is of a different kind fades away, the goal is quickly attained; in this way, even a knowledge lineage long accustomed to beginningless worldly life is transformed.

[tal-a28-v203] When that worldly lineage is destroyed, transcendent knowledge arises and takes on the character of another, noble lineage not accustomed to worldly life.

[tal-a28-v204] The primary and original cause is the teacher's knowledge entering the self, clearly bestowing its own distinctive qualities.

[tal-a28-v205] That knowledge is indeed a fitting material cause; for even when bodies differ, the difference and non-difference that apply to the bodily lineage do not apply in the same way to the lineage of knowledge.

[tal-a28-v206] It is not the same as a yogi animating a corpse-body by will; when a yogi brings life to another body and so on, that does not create the same kind of continuity, since the yogi does not abandon his own body.

[tal-a28-v207] Even if a yogi, without abandoning the body, becomes the basis for various knowledges, that does not change the fact that the lineage of knowledge is primary over the bodily lineage.

[tal-a28-v208] Thus, when there is a mutual lineage of teachers established in the knowledge of Shiva, a threefold structure is recognized: a primary cause and an assisting cause.

[tal-a28-v209] Thus the teacher's group is understood in terms of cause and effect: the teacher is the cause, and his wife is the assisting cause.

[tal-a28-v210] Because one without power would not be eligible for ritual, the outer counterpart of the inner noble power of awareness is ordinarily required.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ya upāyaḥ samucito jñānasantāna eṣa saḥ / kramasphuṭībhavattādṛksadṛśajñānadhārayā galadvijātīyatayā prāpyaṃ śīghraṃ hi labhyate / evaṃ cānādisaṃsārocitavijñānasantateḥ dhvaṃse lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ santānāntaratāṃ śrayet / asaṃsārocitodāratathāvijñānasantateḥ kāraṇaṃ mukhyamādyaṃ tadguruvijñānamātmagam / atyantaṃ svaviśeṣāṇāṃ tatrārpaṇavaśāt sphuṭam upādānaṃ hi tadyuktaṃ dehabhede hi satyapi / dehasantatigau bhedābhedau vijñānasantateḥ na tathātvāya yogīcchāviṣṭaśāvaśarīravat / yoginaḥ paradehādijīvattāpādane nijam dehamatyajato nānājñānopādānatā na kim / tena vijñānasantānaprādhānyādyaunasantateḥ anyonyaṃ gurusantāno yaḥ śivajñānaniṣṭhitaḥ / itthaṃ sthite trayaṃ mukhyaṃ kāraṇaṃ sahakāri ca ekakāraṇakāryaṃ ca vastvityeṣa gurorgaṇaḥ / guruḥ kāraṇamatroktaṃ tatpatnī sahakāriṇī yato niḥśaktikasyāsya na yāge@dhikṛtirbhavet / antaḥsthodārasaṃvittiśakterbāhyāṃ vināpi tām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v211] Just as a yogi may have capacity even without an assisting cause, those born of one cause are brothers; and anyone similar to that may also be regarded in the same way.

[tal-a28-v212] Again, the teacher group is also spoken of through lineage connection; but this primary lineage is always to be worshiped and honored.

[tal-a28-v213] For teachers and others, the days of birth, initiation, and death are significant, because each of these days is a cause connected with knowledge, the means, the body, and so on.

[tal-a28-v214] Thus one's own birthday is said to be a means of knowledge, because it is the cause of the body through which such enjoyment, liberation, and so on become possible.

[tal-a28-v215] The day on which initiation or a similar consecration of one's self takes place should be regarded as a primary birthday, because it marks the birth of the knowledge lineage.

[tal-a28-v216] One's own death day will be an occasional observance for others, because at the time of death one becomes non-different from Shiva.

[tal-a28-v217] There we clearly speak of death's nature: even pervasive Shiva becomes contracted by the seal of self-willed creation.

[tal-a28-v218] By the flood of varied fruit-actions one becomes a body-taker; body-taking is thus tied to womb-body movement.

[tal-a28-v219] When consciousness rises from the void, the first breath-arising occurs in womb-body making, and that lordship returns again.

[tal-a28-v220] The uncontracted lord is called maker of body; he is wind-self in the firm body-machine, by consciousness-self.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sāmarthyaṃ yogino yadvadvināpi sahakāriṇam / ekajanyā bhrātaraḥ syustatsadṛgyastu ko@pi saḥ punaḥ paramparāyogādguruvargo@pi bhaṇyate / mukhya eṣa tu santānaḥ pūjyo mānyaśca sarvadā gurvādīnāṃ ca sambhūtau dīkṣāyāṃ prāyaṇe@pi ca / yadahastaddhi vijñānopāyadehādikāraṇam evaṃ svajanmadivaso vijñānopāya ucyate / tādṛgbhogāpavargādihetordehasya kāraṇam dīkṣādikaśca saṃskāraḥ svātmano yatra cāhni tat / bhavejjanmadinaṃ mukhyaṃ jñānasantānajanmataḥ svakaṃ mṛtidinaṃ yattu tadanyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati / naimittikaṃ mṛto yasmācchivābhinnastadā bhavet tatra prasaṅgānmaraṇasvarūpaṃ brūmahe sphuṭam / vyāpako@pi śivaḥ svecchākḷptasaṅkocamudraṇāt vicitraphalakarmaughavaśāttattaccharīrabhāk / śarīrabhāktvaṃ caitāvadyattadgarbhasthadehagaḥ saṃvitteḥ śūnyarūḍhāyāḥ prathamaḥ prāṇanodayaḥ / garbhasthadehanirmāṇe tasyaiveśvaratā punaḥ asaṅkocasya tanvādikartā teneśa ucyate / sa vāyvātmā dṛḍhe tasmindehayantre cidātmanā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v221] Being driven, it moves like wind in a bellows; therefore it awakens like one risen from deep sleep.

[tal-a28-v222] Gradually with the body breathing becomes stronger; even there, by action-destiny strength, breathing suffers injury.

[tal-a28-v223] It grasps from excess void-cavity consciousness touch; thus gradually the nourished body-breath becomes greatly strong.

[tal-a28-v224] The womb-born body-goer enjoys pleasures made by action; this is said in the cave-named scripture by the cool-ray-crowned.

[tal-a28-v225] As a householder dwells in a house he has made, so the embodied one, devoid of action-qualities, dwells in a body he has made.

[tal-a28-v226] The mere flicker, even he, is called pre-partial; the clear senses principle is spoken of as whole-self.

[tal-a28-v227] And so forth spoken by Gahvara; from that indeed read much; but when actions are destroyed, the body-machine goes otherwise.

[tal-a28-v228] The breath-machine breaks apart; the body becomes like a wall; contraction and expansion in the nerve-wheels reverse.

[tal-a28-v229] Breaking, drying, moisture, wind, phlegm, fire decrease and increase, and such; whatever crushes the prior state.

[tal-a28-v230] The breaking of the body-machine is said by wise ones; when that machine breaks, consciousness-breathing becomes self-ness.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-preryamāṇo vicarati bhastrāyantragavāyuvat / ataḥ prāggāḍhasaṃsuptotthitavatsa prabuddhyate kramāddehena sākaṃ ca prāṇanā syādbalīyasī / tatrāpi karmaniyatibalātsā prāṇanākṣatām gṛhṇāti śūnyasuṣirasaṃvitsparśādhikatvataḥ / evaṃ krameṇa saṃpuṣṭadehaprāṇabalo bhṛśam bhogānkarmakṛtānbhuṅkte yonyayonijadehagaḥ / uktaṃ ca gahvarābhikhye śāstre śītāṃśumaulinā yathā gṛhaṃ viniṣpādya gṛhī samadhitiṣṭhati / tathā dehī tanuṃ kṛtvā kriyādiguṇavarjitaḥ kiñcitsphuraṇamātraḥ prāgniṣkalaḥ so@pi śabdyate / sphuṭendriyāditattvastu sakalātmeti bhaṇyate ityādi śrīgahvaroktaṃ tata eva paṭhedbahu / kṣaye tu karmaṇāṃ teṣāṃ dehayantre@nyathāgate prāṇayantraṃ vighaṭate dehaḥ syātkuḍyavattataḥ / nāḍīcakreṣu saṅkocavikāsau viparītataḥ bhaṅgaḥ śoṣaḥ klidirvātaśleṣmāgnyapacayoccayaiḥ / ityevamādi yatkiñcit prāksaṃsthānopamardakam dehayantre vighaṭanaṃ tadevoktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ / tasminvighaṭite yantre sā saṃvitprāṇanātmatām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v231] It grasps in a womb-born or other body; in an action-painted body, that body awakens then like one risen from sleep.

[tal-a28-v232] Even for that, enjoyment, destruction, and immortalities occur; creation, maintenance, and destruction arise from action strength.

[tal-a28-v233] Therefore grace, for one following destiny, time, and variety, is that which blossoms in its own nature.

[tal-a28-v234] As knowledge-self, how does it await action-destiny and the like? Because of contracted life, action, time, and destiny await.

[tal-a28-v235] In the form of contraction-loss, how is the cause in grace? Grace is divided into gradual and intense.

[tal-a28-v236] This was spoken in detail before; what need repetitions? By that, initiation and Shiva-knowledge burn the contraction bond.

[tal-a28-v237] At body-end, Shiva indeed; for him there is no staying in another body, even for those descended in truth and followers of Shankara's command.

[tal-a28-v238] Dead in houses of self-born, sage, god, sage, man and other worlds, having reached that city, are initiated by city-lords gradually.

[tal-a28-v239] Having descended into mortal or not, they go to Shiva without rebirth; there self-born are in two ways, some devoted to grace.

[tal-a28-v240] Some serve only the place of their own-duty-come part; among those commanded for grace, the man who dies.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-gṛhṇāti yonije@nyatra vā dehe karmacitrite / sa dehaḥ pratibudhyeta prasuptotthitavattadā tasyāpi bhogataddhānimṛtayaḥ prāgvadeva hi / visṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārā ete karmabalādyataḥ ato niyatikālādivaicitryānuvidhāyinaḥ / anugrahastu yaḥ so@yaṃ svasvarūpe vikasvare jñaptyātmeti kathaṃ karmaniyatyādi pratīkṣate / karmakālaniyatyādi yataḥ saṅkocajīvitam saṅkocahānirūpe@sminkathaṃ heturanugrahe / anugrahaśca kramikastīvraśceti vibhidyate prāk caiṣa vistarātprokta iti kiṃ punaruktibhiḥ / tena dīkṣāśivajñānadagdhasaṅkocabandhanaḥ dehānte śiva eveti nāsya dehāntarasthitiḥ / ye@pi tattvāvatīrṇānāṃ śaṃkarājñānuvartinām svayambhūmunidevarṣimanujādibhuvāṃ gṛhe / mṛtāste tatpuraṃ prāpya pureśairdīkṣitāḥ kramāt martye@vatīrya vā no vā śivaṃ yāntyapunarbhavāḥ / tatra svayambhuvo dvedhā ke@pyanugrahatatparāḥ ke@pi svakṛtyāyātāṃśasthānamātropasevinaḥ / ye@nugrahārthamājñaptāsteṣu yo mriyate naraḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v241] He goes to clear grace without mortal descent, and he who does his own task does not partially abandon that place.

[tal-a28-v242] As gauri practicing austerity in kashmir goes to a cave, or as narahari the lord is in meditation lift.

[tal-a28-v243] Leading vitasta and frightening proud demons, risen in saligrama, as vishnu or shiva of self-enjoying.

[tal-a28-v244] Practicing austerity in badari, nara and narayana, and such gods are established in their own task portions.

[tal-a28-v245] Worshiped gods quickly grant fitting fruit, and those established in their own task part who go to the end of the abode.

[tal-a28-v246] There, having enjoyed enjoyments, they descend among mortals; those descended become part-bearers and that again.

[tal-a28-v247] By initiation, knowledge, practice and sequence they go to shiva selfhood; immobile and mobile animals, beasts in this duality, are dead.

[tal-a28-v248] By purification of own action piercing that world, men and mere beasts taking variegation attain same world without discernment.

[tal-a28-v249] Non-discernment, special unfolding from dullness, and thus immobile beings take increasing state, or.

[tal-a28-v250] They do not attain direct rudra state; that gradually again, in swan and duck filled various tree thicket.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-so@nugrahaṃ sphuṭaṃ yāti vinā martyāvatārataḥ / yastu svakāryaṃ kurvāṇastatsthānaṃ nāṃśatastyajet yathā gaurī tapasyantī kaśmīreṣu guhāgatā / tatraiva vā yathā dhyānoḍḍāre naraharirvibhuḥ vitastāṃ nayato daityāṃstrāsayandṛpta utthitaḥ / sāligrāme yathā viṣṇuḥ śivo vā svopabhoginaḥ tapasyantau badaryāṃ ca naranārāyaṇau tathā / ityevamādayo devāḥ svakṛtyāṃśasthitāstathā ārādhitāḥ svocitaṃ tacchīghraṃ vidadhate phalam / svakṛtyāṃśasthitānāṃ ca dhāmni ye@ntaṃ vrajanti te tatra bhogāṃstathā bhuktvā martyeṣvavatarantyapi / martyāvatīrṇāste tattadaṃśakāstanmayāḥ punaḥ taddīkṣājñānacaryādikramādyānti śivātmatām / sthāvarādyāstiryagantāḥ paśavo@smindvaye mṛtāḥ svakarmasaṃskriyāvedhāttalloke citratājuṣaḥ / puṃsāṃ ca paśumātrāṇāṃ sālokyamavivekataḥ avivekastadviśeṣānunmeṣānmauḍhyatastathā / sthāvarādyāstathābhāvamuttarottaratāṃ ca vā prapadyante na te sākṣādrudratāṃ tāṃ kramātpunaḥ / haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇe nānātarukulākule

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v251] Thus this is said in scriptures; from that only in city city I speak field measure declared in auspicious all knowledge.

[tal-a28-v252] From linga hundred hands field when teacher established self-born being; thousand but half when sage joined.

[tal-a28-v253] When truth-knower establishes linga, fruit is self-born-like; when non-truth-knower, then teacher establishes linga then.

[tal-a28-v254] Again rite becomes fault, indeed otherwise both corrupting: if opinion says I other, supreme self other, shiva other.

[tal-a28-v255] Not liberates, not; liberated and all self-filled because; therefore by truth-knower whatever established linga is supreme.

[tal-a28-v256] That only as abode, resort for enjoyment and liberation; said in shri ratnamala, knowing time arrived.

[tal-a28-v257] Liberation seeker should not fear, should go abandon body without doubt; or deceive time in pilgrimage abode merits, beloved.

[tal-a28-v258] This path is of non-yogis; yogi should deceive by yoga; if incapable, being should go to field abode.

[tal-a28-v259] In pilgrimage, from refuge of that, deception arises; by this and in earth etc, in principles by practice yoga.

[tal-a28-v260] So far siddhi enjoying also said; for liberation field usefulness; in right knower account previously will be taught.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ityetadāgameṣūktaṃ tata eva pure pure / kṣetramānaṃ bruve śrīmatsarvajñānādiṣūditam liṅgāddhastaśataṃ kṣetramācāryasthāpite sati / svayambhūte sahasraṃ tu tadardhamṛṣiyojite tattvavitsthāpite liṅge svayambhūsadṛśaṃ phalam / atattvavidyadācāryo liṅgaṃ sthāpayate tadā punarvidhirbhaveddoṣo hyanyathobhayadūṣakaḥ / ahamanyaḥ parātmānyaḥ śivo@nya iti cenmatiḥ na mocayenna muktaśca sarvamātmamayaṃ yataḥ / tasmāttattvavidā yadyatsthāpitaṃ liṅgamuttamam tadevāyatanatvena saṃśrayedbhuktimuktaye / uktaṃ śrīratnamālāyāṃ jñātvā kālamupasthitam mokṣārthī na bhayaṃ gacchettyajeddehamaśaṅkitaḥ / tīrthāyatanapuṇyeṣu kālaṃ vā vañcayetpriye ayogināmayaṃ panthā yogī yogena vañcayet / vañcane tvasamarthaḥ san kṣetramāyatanaṃ vrajet tīrthe samāśrayāttasya vañcanaṃ tu vijāyate / anena ca dharādyeṣu tattveṣvabhyāsayogataḥ tāvatsiddhijuṣo@pyuktā muktyai kṣetropayogitā / samyagjñānini vṛttāntaḥ purastāttūpadekṣyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v261] Of beasts this account; those initiated in that principle go to nearness to that lord by own fitness yoga.

[tal-a28-v262] Born from fitness dependence, whose tendency where only, he there only should be appointed, from city lord upward purity sharer.

[tal-a28-v263] Thus previously said auspicious; in auspicious svayambhuva also, who where desires enjoyments, he there only appointed.

[tal-a28-v264] Siddhi bearer, mantra power, etc., described elsewhere; those in principle knowledge, mantra, practice, etc.

[tal-a28-v265] When those knowers die, they attain union with that Rudra. Yet even after reaching that union, the form it takes varies according to their own latent impressions.

[tal-a28-v266] In this way, descents that come from a portion of that Rudra can be highly varied. This is widely reported in the Siddhanta scriptures, in the Puranas, and elsewhere.

[tal-a28-v267] Even when all are equally descents of Rudra, their actions and experiences differ. This is because the form of any being is made up of many different powers.

[tal-a28-v268] A being is not something apart from its powers; it exists only as their collection. Therefore, what descends as a portion from Rudra and the rest is a particular configuration of powers.

[tal-a28-v269] A portion descends so that the task suited to it can clearly be accomplished. The verse then turns to those who, after receiving initiation at a lower level, abandon their faith in it for something higher.

[tal-a28-v270] Those who die fixed in that lower level still attain its highest reach. But those who let go of that elevation attain what lies above it.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-paśūnāmeṣa vṛttānto ye tu tattattvadīkṣitāḥ / te tadīśasamīpatvaṃ yānti svaucityayogataḥ yogyatāvaśasaṃjātā yasya yatraiva vāsanā / sa tatraiva niyoktavyaḥ pureśāccordhvaśuddhibhāk iti śrīpūrvakathitaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuve@pica / yo yatrābhilaṣedbhogānsa tatraiva niyojitaḥ siddhibhāṅmantrasāmarthyādityādyanyatra varṇitam / ye tu tattattvavijñānamantracaryādivartinaḥ mṛtāste tatra tadrudrasayuktvaṃ yānti kovidāḥ / teṣāṃ sayuktvaṃ yātānāmapi saṃskārato nijāt tathā tathā vicitraḥ syādavatārastadaṃśataḥ / siddhāntādau purāṇeṣu tathāca śrūyate bahu tulye rudrāvatāratve citratvaṃ karmabhogayoḥ / anekaśaktikhacitaṃ yato bhāvasya yadvapuḥ śaktibhyo@rthāntaraṃ naiṣa tatsamūhādṛte bhavet / tena śaktisamūhākhyāt tasmādrudrādyadaṃśataḥ kṛtyaṃ taducitaṃ siddhyet soṃ@śo@vatarati sphuṭam / ye cādharaprāptadīkṣāstadāsthānujjhitāḥ pare tattve mṛtāḥ kāṣṭhavatte@dhare@pyutkarṣabhāginaḥ / ye tūjjhitatadutkarṣāste taduttarabhāginaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v271] Even those initiated into a higher level, if they lack sufficient discernment, may reach only a lower end of it. Still, they partake of the fruit of that initiation.

[tal-a28-v272] Such people do not abandon their faith in that initiation, even if it rests on scriptural authority. Lacking discernment, they hold to it on the strength of scripture and common repute.

[tal-a28-v273] The Supreme Lord taught that one who is merely a bound soul attains the same world, the initiated attains nearness, and one who is devoted to that path attains union.

[tal-a28-v274] If someone who follows the higher teaching abandons faith in it through doubt, then even when going to its abode he obtains no fruit at all.

[tal-a28-v275] On this point the God of gods said that for such a person initiation, knowledge, and even sacred places are in vain, and so on, as explained in detail elsewhere.

[tal-a28-v276] Even if someone is unfit at first, if he remains steadfast in the abode of Shiva, then through that enduring bond of faith he will later obtain that very fruit.

[tal-a28-v277] Merit gained from places like rivers, mountains, and pools is not the highest thing at death. Those who die with that merit enjoy the pleasures of heaven.

[tal-a28-v278] Those who had gained knowledge and discernment, but near death take refuge in lower abodes, become veiled there.

[tal-a28-v279] This is described as a defilement of their knowledge and may indeed count as sin. The established view is that it is removed through the proper sequence of initiation into the lords of those respective realms.

[tal-a28-v280] But those who, in mind and conduct, defile initiation, sacred abodes, and knowledge all go to hell.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ye@pyūrdhvatattvadīkṣāste vinā tāvadvivekataḥ / prāptādharāntā api taddīkṣāphalasubhāginaḥ atyaktāsthā hi te tatra dīkṣāyāmapi śāstritāt / vinā vivekādāsthāṃ te śritā lokaprasiddhitaḥ paśumātrasya sālokyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ dīkṣitasya tu / tatparasya tu sāyujyamityuktaṃ parameśinā yastūrdhvaśāstragastatra tyaktāsthaḥ saṃśayena saḥ / vrajannāyatanaṃ naiva phalaṃ kiñcitsamaśnute uktaṃ tadviṣayaṃ caitaddevadevena yadvṛthā / dīkṣā jñānaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tasyetyādi savistaram yastu tāvadayogyo@pi tathāste sa śivālaye / paścādāsthānibandhena tāvadeva phalaṃ bhajet nadīnagahradaprāyaṃ yacca puṇyaṃ na tanmṛtau / utkṛṣṭaṃ tanmṛtānāṃ tu svargabhogopabhogitā ye punaḥ prāptavijñānavivekā maraṇāntike / adharāyataneṣvāsthāṃ śritāste@tra tirohitāḥ tajjñānadūṣaṇoktaṃ yatteṣāṃ syātkila pātakam / tattatpureśadīkṣādikramānnaśyediti sthitiḥ dīkṣāyatanavijñānadūṣiṇo ye tu cetasā / ācaranti ca tatte@tra sarve nirayagāminaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v281] The loss of one's bond of faith in knowledge, sacred abodes, and initiation is to be recognized by disturbed activities, and those activities are of two kinds.

[tal-a28-v282] Some disturbances never arise when a person is healthy and appear only in illness, caused by bodily imbalance. These amount only to the experience of that condition.

[tal-a28-v283] Bodily imbalance may awaken old worldly impressions, and they may slip in through temporary openings. But if they have mostly been burned by knowledge, they cannot grow again.

[tal-a28-v284] But in those oriented toward isolation, some impressions never appear in good health and yet open up in illness. These arise from the descent of power.

[tal-a28-v285] Ordinary worldly impressions are formed by long, deep habituation from the past. As the Lord of Serpents said in the sutra, they appear in those openings.

[tal-a28-v286] In those oriented toward isolation, some cognitions arise that were never practiced before. Because of the nature of transmigration, these cannot come from habit and must come from the descent of power.

[tal-a28-v287] These disturbed activities, when aggravated by bodily imbalance, lack settled certainty and reflective awareness, and they resemble the behavior of someone asleep or intoxicated.

[tal-a28-v288] Even if disturbed behavior seems perverse and appears to defile knowledge, initiation, or the teacher, it should not be taken as true veiling when it has not taken root in the heart.

[tal-a28-v289] For this very reason, even an awakened person, while still in the body, may undergo karma-born experiences at death, such as visions of Yama's servants, snakes, and the like.

[tal-a28-v290] This alone does not mean he is not liberated, for death is an experience just like birth and ongoing life. Therefore death can be of two kinds, involving pain or pleasure.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-jñānāyatanadīkṣādāvāsthābandhaparicyutiḥ / vyāpāravyāhṛtairjñeyā tānyapi dvividhāni ca yāni jātucidapyeva svāsthye nodamiṣanpunaḥ / asvāsthye dhātudoṣotthānyeva tadbhogamātrakam dhātudoṣācca saṃsārasaṃskārāste prabodhitāḥ / chidragā api bhūyiṣṭhajñānadagdhā na rohiṇaḥ ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ svāsthye@nunmiṣitāḥ sadā / asvāsthye conmiṣantyete saṃskārāḥ śaktipātataḥ yataḥ sāṃsārikāḥ pūrvagāḍhābhyāsopasaṃskṛtāḥ / ityūce bhujagādhīśastacchidreṣviti sūtrataḥ ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ pratyayāste na jātucit / abhyastāḥ saṃsṛterbhāvāttenaite śaktipātataḥ vyāpāravyāhṛtaistena dhātudoṣaprakopitaiḥ / aprāptaniścayāmarśaiḥ suptamattopamānakaiḥ viparītairapi jñānadīkṣāgurvādidūṣakaiḥ / tirobhāvo na vijñeyo hṛdaye rūḍhyabhāvataḥ ata eva prabuddho@pi karmotthānbhogarūpiṇaḥ / yamakiṅkarasarpādipratyayāndehago bhajet naitāvatā na mukto@sau mṛtirbhogo hi janmavat / sthitivacca tato duḥkhasukhābhyāṃ maraṇaṃ dvidhā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v291] So, just as the varied pleasures and pains of life do not destroy the liberated state of an awakened person, those same kinds of experiences at death do not destroy it either.

[tal-a28-v292] But those yogins who have become well established in a particular principle fix their mind on that very principle and, without doubt, go to it.

[tal-a28-v293] This is stated in the revered Svacchanda Tantra, beginning with the teaching about those who die through concentration on fragrance, and likewise the Malini scripture gives the fruits of the various concentrations.

[tal-a28-v294] For those who quickly abandon the body through concentrations, as if entering another body, there is no experience that can properly be called death.

[tal-a28-v295] The ordinary experience of death consists in a cutting shock at the vital points, delusion spreading through the senses, and a mental sinking into darkness. None of this is found in these yogins.

[tal-a28-v296] For the yogin maintains mental effort, establishing an I-sense in another body, as long as the movement of intellect continues there.

[tal-a28-v297] The circle of breath, dependent on that same process, moves along the path, and by that very means the circle of senses in the other body becomes awakened.

[tal-a28-v298] Just as bees rise when the bee-king rises and settle when he settles, so all the activities of the senses follow the mind.

[tal-a28-v299] Therefore, when he moves into another body, there is no inward merging of the senses as in ordinary death. Instead, a subtle continuity arises again, like a body.

[tal-a28-v300] Thus, for yogins who move into other bodies and likewise for those who move within bodies formed of various principles, there is no delusion.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ato yathā prabuddhasya sukhaduḥkhavicitratāḥ / sthitau na ghnanti muktatvaṃ maraṇe@pi tathaiva tāḥ ye punaryoginaste@pi yasmiṃstattve subhāvitāḥ / cittaṃ niveśayantyeva tattattvaṃ yāntyaśaṅkitāḥ śrīsvacchande tataḥ proktaṃ gandhadhāraṇayā mṛtāḥ / ityādi mālinīśāstre dhāraṇānāṃ tathā phalam eteṣāṃ maraṇābhikhyo bhogo nāsti tu ye tanum / dhāraṇābhistyajantyāśu paradehapraveśavat etāvānmṛtibhogo hi marmacchinmūḍhatākṣagā / dhvāntābilatvaṃ manasi taccaiteṣu na vidyate tathāhi mānasaṃ yatnaṃ tāvatsamadhitiṣṭhati / ahaṃrūḍhyā pare dehe yāvatsyādbuddhisaṃcaraḥ prāṇacakraṃ tadāyattamapi saṃcarate pathā / tenaivātaḥ prabuddhyeta paradehe@kṣacakrakam makṣikā makṣikārājaṃ yathotthitamanūtthitāḥ / sthitaṃ cānuviśantyevaṃ cittaṃ sarvākṣavṛttayaḥ ato@sya paradehādisaṃcāre nāsti melanam / akṣāṇāṃ madhyagaṃ sūkṣmaṃ syādetaddehavatpunaḥ evaṃ paraśarīrādicāriṇāmiva yoginām / tattattattvaśarīrāntaścāriṇāṃ nāsti mūḍhatā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v301] These yogins should be known as twofold: worldly and initiated. The former become Shiva gradually, while the latter do so merely through experiencing that state.

[tal-a28-v302] Initiation, being divided by many higher and lower distinctions, yields varied fruits for yogins.

[tal-a28-v303] But those who are knowers are of two kinds, according to whether their knowledge trembles or not. Among them, those whose knowledge trembles clearly become Shiva at the end of the body.

[tal-a28-v304] Because knowledge has arisen in them, but it is not very clear due to association with other conceptual thoughts, nor is it uprooted in its nature.

[tal-a28-v305] Therefore, the conceptual thought that arises in the body from carelessness necessarily perishes when the body falls, and that supreme knowledge is then recognized.

[tal-a28-v306] That knowledge, not destroyed within but standing as latent conceptual traces, having reached ripeness, indeed shines forth when the obstruction is removed.

[tal-a28-v307] But those whose nature is well-practiced knowledge, who are always of the nature of Shiva, are indeed liberated while living; for them there is no question at all at the time of death.

[tal-a28-v308] For just as there is no question about the living-liberated being happy, unhappy, or deluded while they live, so too there is no such question at death.

[tal-a28-v309] The Supreme Lord said this in the holy Ratnamala scripture, and so did the Lord Ahi, bearer of the burden of supporting the universe, in his own scripture.

[tal-a28-v310] Whether in a street, amid urine and feces, in an outcaste's house, in hell, or in a cremation ground, whether with thought or without thought, the knower obtains liberation at the end.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-te cāpi dvividhā jñeyā laukikā dīkṣitāstathā / pūrve śivāḥ syuḥ kramaśaḥ pare tadbhogamātrataḥ dīkṣāpyūrdhvādharānekabhedayojanikāvaśāt / bhidyamānā yogināṃ syādvicitraphaladāyinī ye tu vijñāninaste@tra dvedhā kampretaratvataḥ / tatra ye kampravijñānāste dehānted śivāḥ sphuṭam yato vijñānameteṣāmutpannaṃ naca susphuṭam / vikalpāntarayogena nacāpyunmūlitātmakam ato dehe pramādottho vikalpo dehapātataḥ / naśyedavaśyaṃ taccāpi budhyate jñānamuttamam saṃskārakalpanātiṣṭhadadhvastīkṛtamantarā / prāptapākaṃ saṃvarīturapāye bhāsate hi tat ye tu svabhyastavijñānamayāḥ śivamayāḥ sadā / jīvanmuktā hi te naiṣāṃ mṛtau kāpi vicāraṇā yathāhi jīvanmuktānāṃ sthitau nāsti vicāraṇā / sukhiduḥkhivimūḍhatve, mṛtāvapi tathā na sā śrīratnamālāśāstre taduvāca parameśvaraḥ / svaśāstre cāpyahīśāno viśvādhāradhurandharaḥ rathyāntare mūtrapurīṣamadhye caṇḍālagehe niraye śmaśāne / sacintako vā gatacintako vā jñānī vimokṣaṃ labhate@pi cānte

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v311] The words 'even' and 'also' indicate his state of living liberation; the mention of being with thought or without thought refers only to a possible circumstance at that time.

[tal-a28-v312] Whether at a holy place or in an outcaste's house, even if memory is lost, one who abandons the body, being liberated simultaneously with knowledge, attains absolute freedom, with sorrow destroyed.

[tal-a28-v313] The Ananta-verses say that one might suspect good or bad deeds to bind him, but in fact they do not bind him.

[tal-a28-v314] From the word 'even' one might think death with memory intact is possible, but death usually involves lost memory; and if memory was lost before death, what does that matter?

[tal-a28-v315] The optative indicates mere possibility, and the time-expression shows that death is not the cause of liberation.

[tal-a28-v316] Although 'isolation' may raise doubt because a body remains, that body no longer produces difference, so sorrowlessness is established.

[tal-a28-v317] Just as connection with other bodies does not differentiate him, so too connection with his own body does not differentiate the living-liberated person.

[tal-a28-v318] Therefore, for one who is non-different from Śiva and has set aside all universal forms, there is no real difference whether he is in a body or not.

[tal-a28-v319] Even so, because suspicion based on old impressions of difference may persist, the text now speaks of aloneness; or else it does so from another standpoint.

[tal-a28-v320] Those things do not know him as different, and he is not known as different by them; such a one is called liberated. The revered Traiśirasa also speaks of a state beyond the pair of sun and moon.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-apiceti dhvanirjīvanmuktatāmasya bhāṣate / sacintācintakatvoktiretāvatsaṃbhavasthitim tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtirapi parityajeddeham / jñānasamakālamuktaḥ kaivalyaṃ yāti hataśokaḥ anantakārikā caiṣā prāhedaṃ bandhakaṃ kila / sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cāsya śaṅkyaṃ taccāsya no bhavet apiśabdādaluptasmṛtyā vā saṃbhāvyate kila / mṛtirnaṣṭasmṛtereva mṛteḥ prāk sāstu kiṃ tayā liṅca saṃbhāvanāyāṃ syādiyatsaṃbhāvyate kila / saca kāladhvaniḥ prāha mṛtermuktāvahetutām kaivalyamiti cāśaṅkāpadaṃ yāpyabhavattanuḥ / bhedapradatvenaiṣāpi dhvastā tena viśokatā paradehādisaṃbandho yathā nāsya vibhedakaḥ / tathā svadehasaṃbandho jīvanmuktasya yadyapi ataśca na viśeṣo@sya viśvākṛtinirākṛteḥ / śivābhinnasya dehe vā tadabhāve@pi vā kila tathāpi prācyatadbhedasaṃskārāśaṅkanasthiteḥ / adhunoktaṃ kevalatvaṃ yadvā mātrantarāśrayāt tānyenaṃ na vidurbhinnaṃ taiḥ sa mukto@bhidhīyate / śrīmattraiśirase@pyuktaṃ sūryendupuṭavarjite

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v321] It is a state where disgust and its opposite are broken, steady on all sides like a pillar, free from all calamity, and beyond valid cognition and mental constructs.

[tal-a28-v322] Absorbed in that inner awareness, one may still act yet remain unstained. The key example is space in a pot: even when the pot is broken, space is not destroyed.

[tal-a28-v323] Just as space does not perish when the pot is broken, so this self does not perish; the knower becomes Śiva-natured, independent, and extends into all things.

[tal-a28-v324] For him there is neither mere being nor non-being, neither fixed form nor mental construction. This same point was spoken by the teacher in the Gītā.

[tal-a28-v325] Whatever state one remembers while leaving the body at the end, that alone one attains, because one has always been shaped by dwelling on that state.

[tal-a28-v326] Therefore remember me at all times and fight. When sattva is predominant, the one who dissolves then goes upward.

[tal-a28-v327] If one dissolves in rajas and tamas, one goes deluded into a karmic birth; then there is confusion of the senses and distress marked by labored breathing.

[tal-a28-v328] Experiences like these occur in the body and are not the same as abandoning the body; the real abandonment is only that single final moment consisting of the last breath.

[tal-a28-v329] The instant immediately after which the body becomes like wood or a wall is the fractional moment of abandoning the body, the moment that separates one from it.

[tal-a28-v330] At that very moment, free from the body's pleasure and pain, one remembers whatever is awakened by prior impressions.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-jugupsābhāvabhaṅgasthe sarvataḥ stambhavatsthite / sarvavyāpattirahite pramāṇapratyayātige tasminbodhāntare līnaḥ karmakartāpyanañjanaḥ / pradhānaṃ ghaṭa ākāśa ātmā maṣṭe ghaṭe@pi kham na naśyettadvadevāsāvātmā śivamayo bhavet / svatantro@vasthito jñānī prasaretsarvavastuṣu tasya bhāvo nacābhāvaḥ saṃsthānaṃ naca kalpanā / etadevāntarāgūrya gururgītāsvabhāṣata yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram / taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca / yadā sattve vivṛddhe tu pralīnastvūrdhvagastadā kramādrajastamolīnaḥ karmayonivimūḍhagaḥ / tatrendriyāṇāṃ saṃmohaśvāsāyāsaparītatā ityādimṛtibhogo@yaṃ dehe na tyajanaṃ tanoḥ / yastvasau kṣaṇa evaikaścaramaḥ prāṇanātmakaḥ yadanantaramevaiṣa dehaḥ syātkāṣṭhakuḍyavat / sā dehatyāgakālāṃśakalā dehaviyoginī tata eva hi taddehasukhaduḥkhādikojjhitā / tasyāṃ yadeva smarati prāksaṃskāraprabodhataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v331] Because of unseen merit, repeated practice, intensity, descent of power, and similar causes, one attains that very form, whether happy, suffering, or deluded.

[tal-a28-v332] Or else, if one attains a state free from pleasure and pain, or one of bliss, why is that? Because that is what one remembers in consciousness.

[tal-a28-v333] Whatever shone forth most strongly before becomes decisive, because this body is established in consciousness; what consciousness previously took as its basis through identification becomes that basis.

[tal-a28-v334] This is what is called absorption in sattva, rajas, tamas, or in knowable things like blue and yellow: consciousness takes up a form that was previously constructed.

[tal-a28-v335] Consciousness, by taking its stand, fully makes something into a basis; therefore, even if a body is something merely established, it differs from an inert thing like a wall.

[tal-a28-v336] The body is distinct because it comes first among all things that consciousness establishes. Other things may also be identified with, but that is not known in the same foundational way.

[tal-a28-v337] Because knowables depend on the body, and the body is constant and non-deviating, prior death and birth belong to that same body.

[tal-a28-v338] By memory, whose impressions come from past experience, Kallata our lineage teacher reasons thus.

[tal-a28-v339] In bodily indistinction, breath-firmness is stated as the cause; otherwise, what is the cause of breath-firmness?

[tal-a28-v340] The question does not subside in bodily indistinction; remembering, one attains that form in the cause.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-adṛṣṭābhyāsabhūyastvaśaktipātādihetukāt / tadeva rūpamabhyeti sukhiduḥkhivimūḍhakam yadvā niḥsukhaduḥkhādi yadi vānandarūpakam / kasmādeti tadevaiṣa yataḥ smarati saṃvidi prāk prasphuredyadadhikaṃ deho@sau cidadhiṣṭhiteḥ / yadeva prāgadhiṣṭhānaṃ citā tādātmyavṛttitaḥ saivātra līnatā proktā sattve rajasi tāmase / nīlapītādike jñeye yataḥ prākkalpitāṃ tanum adhiṣṭhāyaiva saṃvittiradhiṣṭhānaṃ karotyalam / ato@dhiṣṭheyamātrasya śarīratve@pi kuḍyataḥ dehasyāsti viśeṣo yatsarvādhiṣṭheyapūrvatā / tādātmyavṛttiranyeṣāṃ tanna satyapi vedyate vedyānāṃ kintu dehasya nityāvyabhicaritvataḥ / sā ca tasyaiva dehasya pūrvamṛtyantajanmanā smṛtyā prācyānubhavanakṛtasaṃskāracitrayā / yuktyānayāsmatsantānaguruṇā kallaṭena yat dehāviśeṣe prāṇākhyadārḍhyaṃ heturudīritam / tadyuktamanyathā prāṇadārḍhye ko heturekataḥ dehatvasyāviśeṣe@pītyeṣa praśno na śāmyati / smaranniti śatā hetau tadrūpaṃ pratipadyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v341] The body is remembered before because it was previously established and shining; therefore final remembering occurs in all-knowing mothers.

[tal-a28-v342] Determination of another body is never accessible; clear memory of relatives, drinks, and so forth does not prove it.

[tal-a28-v343] Memory is neither attached to another body nor final, because a latent impression will awaken at the end of the body.

[tal-a28-v344] In bodily existence, clear experience arises from fitness, as the Purana tells through the thirst of a deer calf.

[tal-a28-v345] Some sage dwelling in deer nature has that experience, but it is not a cause for next birth.

[tal-a28-v346] His latent impression is the cause, like crow and palm; he remembers that very thing, as is always said.

[tal-a28-v347] Shaped by that state, he remembers that very thing; thus I am, I will be, and that state is called becoming.

[tal-a28-v348] Becoming of the future is imagined, never of what exists; imagination is declared as gradual making clear.

[tal-a28-v349] Experience of the clear is not imagination; this is clear, as with a newborn child, animal, insect, or tree.

[tal-a28-v350] Even in delusion, prior imagination then became clear, through awakening of impressions at the end of the deluded body.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prāk smaryate yato dehaḥ prākcitādhiṣṭhitaḥ sphuran / ataḥ smaraṇamantyaṃ yattadasarvajñamātṛṣu na jātu gocaro yasmāddehāntaraviniścayaḥ / yattu bandhupriyāputrapānādismaraṇaṃ sphuṭam na taddehāntarāsaṅgi na tadantyaṃ yato bhavet / kasyāpi tu śarīrānte vāsanā yā prabhotsyate dehasattve tadaucityājjāyetānubhavaḥ sphuṭaḥ / yathā purāṇe kathitaṃ mṛgapotakatṛṣṇayā muniḥ ko@pi mṛgībhāvamabhyuvāhādhivāsitaḥ / tatra so@nubhavo heturna janmāntarasūtaye tasyaitadvāsanā hetuḥ kākatālīyavat sa tu / nanu kasmāttadevaiṣa smarati ityāha yatsadā tadbhāvabhāvitastena tadevaiṣa smaratyalam / evamasmi bhaviṣyāmītyeṣa tadbhāva ucyate bhaviṣyato hi bhavanaṃ bhāvyate na sataḥ kvacit / kramātsphuṭatvakaraṇaṃ bhāvanaṃ parikīrtyate sphuṭasya cānubhavanaṃ na bhāvanamidaṃ sphuṭam / tadaharjātabālasya paśoḥ kīṭasya vā taroḥ mūḍhatve@pi tadānīṃ prāgbhāvanā hyabhavatsphuṭā / sā tanmūḍhaśarīrānte saṃskārapratibodhanāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v351] Through the gate of memory, latent impressions, even across separation of place and so forth, give the result of that body's variety.

[tal-a28-v352] Because memory and impression have immediacy and one form, by such ascent of experience, even clear experience is imagined.

[tal-a28-v353] Being imagined produces a body similar to that lineage, together with such relatives, sons, friends, and so forth.

[tal-a28-v354] It appears even in the other world, from a latent-impression sequence like a dream, with other mothers, relatives, sons, and so forth.

[tal-a28-v355] This is known; he said it and knows for now. Let it be known in the crowd of activity and utterance, in the group of other mothers.

[tal-a28-v356] In dream he is not; this statement lacks speech and proof, while these are seen awake by me.

[tal-a28-v357] Let it be dream; this is false by the force of cognizer speech, for I see in dream, but no cognizers.

[tal-a28-v358] They neither grieve nor see me; what proof is here, because all inferences rest in self-experience.

[tal-a28-v359] Existence of another cognizer rests in consciousness, not located in that; existence of pot and so forth rests in consciousness, not located in that.

[tal-a28-v360] Similarly, in another mother this rests in consciousness, not located in that; therefore whatever is imagined is indeed that very thing.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-smṛtidvāreṇa taddehavaicitryaphaladāyinī / deśādivyavadhāne@pi vāsanānāmudīritāt ānantaryaikarūpatvātsmṛtisaṃskārayorataḥ / tathānubhavanārūḍhyā sphuṭasyāpi tu bhāvitā bhāvyamānā na kiṃ sūte tatsantānasadṛgvapuḥ / tattādṛktādṛśairbandhuputramitrādibhiḥ saha bhāsate@pi pare loke svapnavadvāsanākramāt / nanu mātrantarairbandhuputrādyaistattathā na kim vedyate ka idaṃ prāha sa tāvadveda vedyatām / vyāpāravyāhṛtivrātavedye mātrantaravraje svapne nāsti sa ityeṣā vākpramāṇavivarjitā / ya evaite tu dṛśyante jāgratyete mayekṣitāḥ svapna ityastu mithyaitattatpramātṛvacobalāt / yānapaśyamahaṃ svapne pramātṝṃste na kecana na śocanti na cekṣante māmityatrāsti kā pramā / yataḥ sarvānumānānāṃ svasaṃvedananiṣṭhitau pramātrantarasadbhāvaḥ saṃvinniṣṭho na tadgataḥ / ghaṭāderastitā saṃvinniṣṭhitā natu tadgatā tadvanmātrantare@pyeṣā saṃvinniṣṭhā na tadgatā / tena sthitamidaṃ yadyadbhāvyate tattadeva hi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v361] At the end of the body, awakening occurs; if not, such awakening would not be possible, for in the final moment one purified by hearing brahma-knowledge awakens.

[tal-a28-v362] The creature is liberated, as said, from the strength of prior impressions, through particles, inner word, remembrance, and the fourth end.

[tal-a28-v363] From a quarter, from a whole half-verse, from what immediately follows, and from the absorbed word, all that stated meaning is true reality.

[tal-a28-v364] Not knowing this, however, all who cling to kusha and kasha vary; some follow one order, some another.

[tal-a28-v365] They abandon two different orders and particles, and explain the seventh case; all that is not suitable in joining.

[tal-a28-v366] And what is shown is not false nor mind-confusing; this true reality of departure is from Shri Shambhunatha.

[tal-a28-v367] By that, fear of death perishes; knowing death's true reality, nectar arises from the consciousness treasury; if gods drink when poison is swallowed here, then your Shiva-nature is certain.

[tal-a28-v368] Even a worldly festival indeed produces joy resembling waves of the consciousness ocean; that too is like a parvan.

[tal-a28-v369] By this, parvans are explained in disaster, destruction, joy, and so on; by that, deity worship is especially important there too.

[tal-a28-v370] The wonder from city agitation gives firmness to one's own consciousness in self-power; special worship is on the day of its gain.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dehānte budhyate no cet syādanyādṛkprabodhanam / tathāhyantyakṣaṇe brahmavidyākarṇanasaṃskṛtaḥ mucyate janturityuktaṃ prāksaṃskārabalatvataḥ / nipātābhyāmantaśabdātsmaraṇācchaturantyataḥ pādācca nikhilādardhaślokācca samanantarāt / līnaśabdācca sarvaṃ taduktamarthasatattvakam ajñātvaitattu sarve@pi kuśakāśāvalambinaḥ / yattadorvyatyayaṃ kecitkecidanyādṛśaṃ kramam bhinnakramau nipātau ca tyajatīti ca saptamīm / vyācakṣate tacca sarvaṃ nopayogyuktayojane naca taddarśitaṃ mithyā svāntasammohadāyakam / taditthaṃprāyaṇasyaitattattvaṃ śrīśambhunāthataḥ adhigamyoditaṃ tena mṛtyorbhītirvinaśyati / viditamṛtisatattvāḥ saṃvidambhonidhānādacalahṛdayavīryākarṣaniṣpīḍanottham / amṛtamiti nigīrṇe kālakūṭe@tra devā yadi pivatha tadānīṃ niścitaṃ vaḥ śivatvam utsavo@pi hi yaḥ kaścillaukikaḥ so@pi saṃmadam / saṃvidabdhitaraṅgābhaṃ sūte tadapi parvavat etena ca vipaddhvaṃsapramodādiṣu parvatā / vyākhyātā tena tatrāpi viśeṣāddevatārcanam purakṣobhādyadbhutaṃ yattatsvātantrye svasaṃvidaḥ / dārḍhyadāyīti tallābhadine vaiśeṣikārcanam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v371] The yogini assembly is twofold, by force and by love; holes are protected in the east, desire-conduct in the north.

[tal-a28-v372] That will be shown in the mantra-extraction context of both; from the yogini assembly this subjection, knowledge is attained.

[tal-a28-v373] By that, that parvan and likewise union of one's own lineage etc.; consciousness is all-self, but she contracts in body difference etc.

[tal-a28-v374] In assembly, blooming from mutual collision reflection, the rising flood of one's own rays is reflected in consciousness.

[tal-a28-v375] Shining like many mirrors, effortlessly for all; therefore in song and the like, in a large assembly.

[tal-a28-v376] The delight in the all-pervading state is not of one alone; bliss-full consciousness is for each, and she thus attains unity.

[tal-a28-v377] In dance and similar objects, having obtained full bliss state, she attains it here from absence of jealousy, envy, and contraction causes.

[tal-a28-v378] The blooming, unobstructed consciousness-bliss yogini is obstructed in a non-pervading state when something stays there.

[tal-a28-v379] When established by consciousness of a different kind, like touching a cavity, therefore in wheel worship and the like, different-kind non-pervading matter is relevant.

[tal-a28-v380] Indeed one should not introduce the cause of consciousness contraction; as many bodies as limbs would be fully filled.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yoginīmelako dvedhā haṭhataḥ priyatastathā / prācye cchidrāṇi saṃrakṣetkāmacāritvamuttare sa ca dvayo@pi mantroddhṛtprasaṅge darśayiṣyate / yoginīmelakāccaiṣo@vaśyaṃ jñānaṃ prapadyate tena tatparva tadvacca svasantānādimelanam / saṃvitsarvātmikā dehabhedādyā saṅkucettu sā melake@nyonyasaṅghaṭṭapratibimbādvikasvarā / ucchalannijaraśmyoghaḥ saṃvitsu pratibimbitaḥ bahudarpaṇavaddīptaḥ sarvāyetāpyayatnataḥ / ata eva gītagītaprabhṛtau bahuparṣadi yaḥ sarvatanmayībhāve hlādo natvekakasya saḥ / ānandanirbharā saṃvitpratyekaṃ sā tathaikatām nṛttādau viṣaye prāptā pūrṇānandatvamaśnute / īrṣyāsūyādisaṅkocakāraṇābhāvato@tra sā vikasvarā niṣpratighaṃ saṃvidānandayoginī / atanmaye tu kasmiṃścittatrasthe pratihanyate sthapuṭasparśavatsaṃvidvijātīyatayā sthite / ataścakrārcanādyeṣu vijātīyamatanmayam naiva praveśayetsaṃvitsaṅkocananibandhanam / yāvantyeva śarīrāṇi svāṅgavatsyuḥ sunirbharām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v381] Having entered one consciousness in the wheel, one should worship that many; if entered by negligence, contraction should not follow from that.

[tal-a28-v382] Commenced own conduct should be practiced together by that; if pierced by your grace power, he becomes that-pervading.

[tal-a28-v383] The left-pierced one, however, should be blamed afterwards and even struck; as said at first in Shrimat Picuma, protect with effort.

[tal-a28-v384] For one who has entered, inquiry should not be caused; but one established in worldly conduct, when such a one has entered, he is that.

[tal-a28-v385] Without omitting that observance, one should worship the circle again. Now I will speak of the stated order for the teacher's explanation of scripture.

[tal-a28-v386] In the Devīyāmala and related scriptures, the moon-crested Lord describes one who knows ritual procedure and its collections, one who knows scripture, and one who knows the meaning of the compendia.

[tal-a28-v387] A teacher who knows the meaning of all scriptures is taught as distinct. But in any given scripture, only the one who has thoroughly mastered it himself should give the explanation.

[tal-a28-v388] It should not be done otherwise. But if such a qualified person is entirely unavailable, even then one may act differently. In the revered Bhairava lineage, such knowledge of ritual procedure and the rest is also described.

[tal-a28-v389] The mark of a teacher is simply complete knowledge. Yet even that knowledge has inner divisions, according to the differing activities of consciousness.

[tal-a28-v390] In the Devīyāmala, in the section called the fifty-two, it is said that the god himself, wishing to stand as teacher, becomes tenfold.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ekāṃ saṃvidamāviśya cakre tāvanti pūjayet / praviṣṭaścetpramādena saṅkocaṃ na vrajettataḥ prastutaṃ svasamācāraṃ tena sākaṃ samācaret / sa tvanugrahaśaktyā cedviddhastattanmayībhavet vāmāviddhastu tannindetpaścāttaṃ ghātayedapi / śrīmatpicumate coktamādau yatnena rakṣayet praveśaṃ saṃpaviṣṭasya na vicāraṃ tu kārayet / lokācārasthito yastu praviṣṭe tādṛśe tu saḥ akṛtvā taṃ samācāraṃ punaścakraṃ prapūjayet / atha vacmi guroḥ śāstravyākhyākramamudāhṛtam devyāyāmalaśāstrādau tuhinābhīśumaulinā / kalpavittatsamūhajñaḥ śāstravitsaṃhitārthavit sarvaśāstrārthavicceti gururbhinno@padiśyate / yo yatra śāstre svabhyastajñāno vyākhyāṃ carettu saḥ nānyathā tadabhāvaścetsarvathā so@pyathācaret / śrībhairavakule coktaṃ kalpādijñatvamīdṛśam gurorlakṣaṇametāvatsaṃpūrṇajñānataiva yā / tatrāpi yāsya cidvṛttikarmibhit sāpyavāntarā devyāyāmala uktaṃ taddvāpañcāśāhva āhnike / deva eva gurutvena tiṣṭhāsurdaśadhā bhavet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v391] Ucchuṣma, Śavara, Caṇḍa, Gumataṅga, Ghora, Antaka, Ugra, Hala, Halaka, Krodhin, and Huluhulu—these are the ten ancient teachers, all consisting of Śiva.

[tal-a28-v392] By the sequence of their own partial modes of consciousness, they assume human bodies. Though their awareness and activity differ from one another, they are all full of knowledge.

[tal-a28-v393] All of them are devoted to the service of meat, wine, union, initiation, worship, and scripture. Their inner difference lies in qualities such as pride, calm, anger, and forbearance.

[tal-a28-v394] Having understood this, the wise student should always request a teacher who knows the complete scripture to give an explanation, doing so with worship beforehand.

[tal-a28-v395] The teacher should give an explanation of such a scripture to his own student, or even to another's student, if the person is fit to hear it—even to a Vaiṣṇava or someone of a lower affiliation.

[tal-a28-v396] A teacher filled with compassion may explain even to a low person, while avoiding the vital secret matters, because the descent of power can occur in many different ways.

[tal-a28-v397] On a smeared, square seat on the ground, one should make three lotuses. On the lotus, one should make the seat of knowledge, measuring six and three finger-widths.

[tal-a28-v398] In the middle one should worship Vāgīśānī; on the south and north, the teachers and Gaṇeśa; and on the lower lotus, the lord of the ritual tradition, using offering water, flowers, and libations.

[tal-a28-v399] Using the offering vessel as in the general rite, the wise teacher should properly satisfy the circle and then give the explanation, beginning with the proper connection.

[tal-a28-v400] By connecting aphorism, word, sentence, chapter, and the whole text in order, and by supporting an unbroken link between what comes before and after, one should lead the sentences forward.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ucchuṣmaśavaracaṇḍagumataṅgaghorāntakograhalahalakāḥ / krodhī huluhulurete daśa guravaḥ śivamayāḥ pūrve te svāṃśacittavṛttikrameṇa pauruṣaśarīramāsthāya / anyonyabhinnasaṃvitkriyā api jñānaparipūrṇāḥ sarve@limāṃsanidhuvanadīkṣārcanaśāstrasevane niratāḥ / abhimānaśamakrodhakṣamādiravāntaro bhedaḥ itthaṃ vijñāya sadā śiṣyaḥ sampūrṇaśāstraboddhāram / vyākhyāyai gurumabhyarthayeta pūjāpuraḥsaraṃ matimān so@pi svaśāsanīye paraśiṣye@pivāpi tādṛśaṃ śāstram / śrotuṃ yogye kuryādvyākhyānaṃ vaiṣṇavādyadhare karuṇārasaparipūrṇo guruḥ punarmarmadhāmaparivarjam / adhame@pi hi vyākuryātsambhāvya hi śaktipātavaicitryam liptāyāṃ bhuvi pīṭhe caturasre paṅkajatrayaṃ kajage / kuryādvidyāpīṭhaṃ syādrasavahnyaṅgulaṃ tvetat madhye vāgīśānīṃ dakṣottarayorgurūngaṇeśaṃ ca / adhare kaje ca kalpeśvaraṃ prapūjyārghapuṣpatarpaṇakaiḥ sāmānyavidhiniyuktārghapātrayogena cakramatha samyak / santarpya vyākhyānaṃ kuryātsambandhapūrvakaṃ matimān sūtrapadavākyapaṭalagranthakramayojanena sambandhāt / avyāhatapūrvāparamupavṛhya nayeta vākyāni

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v401] Using principles such as the frog-leap and the lion-glance as appropriate, one should present the meaning of the scripture clearly, without mixing it up and without breaking the link between what comes before and after.

[tal-a28-v402] One who understands sentences should explain the subject using sound reasoning—such as repetition, contradiction, unwanted consequence, and inference—while keeping it clearly distinct from other matters.

[tal-a28-v403] Whatever point comes up in the explanation should be supported with very firm reasoning, even if it is something that will later be refuted.

[tal-a28-v404] When the subject is taught by first setting out a firmly formed prior view and then resolving it, it quickly enters the student's mind, free from doubt and misunderstanding.

[tal-a28-v405] Whatever language, reasoning, style of discussion, level of absorption, or order becomes a means of awakening for the student, the teacher should adopt that form of explanation.

[tal-a28-v406] After completing the subject being explained, there should be satisfaction and worship in the circle. Another subject may be taught after a chapter, but there should be no idle talk.

[tal-a28-v407] At the end of the explanation, one should ask forgiveness, dismiss everything, and cast the remains into deep water. Worship should be performed especially at the beginning, middle, and end of the scripture.

[tal-a28-v408] At the completion, one should perform special worship for the initiates. Even so, for one whose mind is undivided, there may be no need for expiations.

[tal-a28-v409] Even so, for the grace of those who do not know the truth, one should act as taught in the revered Picu scripture. But if remembrance alone destroys sin, O Lord, how can an expiation rite still be prescribed?

[tal-a28-v410] When the Goddess asked why an expiation rite is declared, the answer is: it is true that remembrance alone, even uttered once, can liberate one here.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-maṇḍūkaplavasiṃhāvalokanādyairyathāyathaṃ nyāyaiḥ / avihatapūrvāparakaṃ śāstrārthaṃ yojayedasaṅkīrṇam tantrāvartanabādhaprasaṅgatarkādibhiśca sannyāyaiḥ / vastu vadedvākyajño vastvantarato viviktatāṃ vidadhat yadyadvyāhṛtipadavīmāyāti tadeva dṛḍhatarairnyāyaiḥ / balavatkuryāddūṣyaṃ yadyapyagre bhaviṣyatsyāt dṛḍharacitapūrvapakṣaproddharaṇapathena vastu yadvācyam / śiṣyamatāvārohati tadāśu saṃśayaviparyayairvikalam bhāṣā nyāyo vādo layaḥ kramo yadyadeti śiṣyasya / sambodhopāyatvaṃ tathaiva gururāśrayedvyākhyām vācyaṃ vastu samāpya pratarpaṇaṃ pūjanaṃ bhaveccakre / punaraparaṃ vastu vadetpaṭalādūrdhvaṃ tu no jalpet vyākhyānte kṣamayitvā visṛjya sarvaṃ kṣipedagādhajale / śāstrādimadhyanidhane viśeṣataḥ pūjanaṃ kuryāt viśeṣapūjanaṃ kuryātsamayebhyaśca niṣkṛtau / avikalpamaterna syuḥ prāyaścittāni yadyapi tathāpyatattvavidvargānugrahāya tathā caret / śrīpicau ca smṛtereva pāpaghnatve kathaṃ vibho prāyaścittavidhiḥ prokta iti devyā pracodite / satyaṃ smaraṇameveha sakṛjjaptaṃ vimocayet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v411] For one who knows remembrance and its truth, liberation from the whole net of action is possible; nevertheless, the rite is enjoined as something to be done for the protection of order.

[tal-a28-v412] Those who do not know the truth and are devoted only to ritual conduct suffer a loss of knowledge when their minds begin to waver.

[tal-a28-v413] Therefore, if one is free from doubt, one should remain discreet and avoid causing confusion when among those who depend on scripture and ritual conduct.

[tal-a28-v414] If confusion of practice arises, one should seek and perform expiation, so that the minds of others do not become unsteady about the meaning of scripture.

[tal-a28-v415] In the rite called Shiva-hand it was formerly enjoined that, by reciting this weapon mantra a hundred times, one is freed, except in the case of killing a woman.

[tal-a28-v416] The revered Ratnamala says, O beloved, that when a vow is transgressed, the destruction of a woman is a great fault leading to everlasting hell.

[tal-a28-v417] For those born in the Kula, an expiation called the wicked knife has been declared; and in the revered earlier text, a purification of the vows is enjoined as follows.

[tal-a28-v418] If an installed sacred object and the like is seen by someone without authority, Malini or Matrika should be recited, up to three hundred thousand times.

[tal-a28-v419] In the revered Brahmayamala it is said that expiation must be performed by a killer of a brahmin, by one who violates the guru's bed, and likewise by one who steals the hero-substance.

[tal-a28-v420] Also included are one who takes the property of the gods or strikes a sacred form, one who breaks the linga, and one who neglects the daily rites and has fallen from his proper measure and equipment.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sarvasmātkarmaṇo jālātsmṛtitattvakalāvidaḥ / tathāpi sthitirakṣārthaṃ kartavyaścodito vidhiḥ atattvavedino ye hi caryāmātraikaniṣṭhitāḥ / teṣāṃ dolāyite citte jñānahāniḥ prajāyate tasmādvikalparahitaḥ saṃvṛtyuparato yadi / śāstracaryāsadāyattaiḥ saṅkaraṃ tadvivarjayet saṅkaraṃ vā samanvicchetprāyaścittaṃ samācaret / yathā teṣāṃ na śāstrārthe dolārūḍhā matirbhavet yatsvayaṃ śivahastākhye vidhau saṃcoditaṃ purā / śataṃ japtvāsya cāstrasya mucyate strīvadhādṛte śaktināśānmahādoṣo narakaṃ śāśvataṃ priye / iti śrīratnamālāyāṃ samayollaṅghane kṛte kulajānāṃ samākhyātā niṣkṛtirduṣṭakartarī / śrīpūrve samayānāṃ tu śodhanāyoditaṃ yathā mālinī mātṛkā vāpi japyā lakṣatrayāntakam / pratiṣṭhitasya pūrāderdarśane@nadhikāriṇā prāyaścittaṃ prakartavyamiti śrībrahmayāmale / brahmaghno gurutalpastho vīradravyaharastathā devadravyahṛdākāraprahartā liṅgabhedakaḥ / nityādilopakṛdbhraṣṭasvakamātrāparicchadaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v421] One who maims Shakti or kills a yogin or knower, or who disrupts the occasional rites, should recite in a doubling sequence beginning with a hundred thousand.

[tal-a28-v422] If someone under a vow, eating moderately and observing celibacy, goes elsewhere to take a messenger woman, deluded by desire, that is an offense.

[tal-a28-v423] Then one should perform a recitation of a hundred thousand, as stated in the Brahmayamala; and at the end of initiation, consecration, and occasional rites, worship of the guru is required.

[tal-a28-v424] According to the teaching of the Siddhayogishvari, it should always be done on the next day: worship of a guru endowed with the previously stated marks, a seer who knows the true principle of the Trika.

[tal-a28-v425] That guru should always be accepted, leaving aside any other, even one present in the circle. One should make a svastika there and place upon it a golden or similar seat.

[tal-a28-v426] Having prepared the seat, one should worship the path present there in its full extent; then, with devotion, one should request the guru to preside there.

[tal-a28-v427] There he should be worshiped with his own mantras, in due order, with flowers, incense, arghya, respectful touching, fine garments, food offerings, and libations.

[tal-a28-v428] After worshiping him fully, even to the directions, the disciple should honor him with gifts, offering all he has and, with devout awareness, even himself.

[tal-a28-v429] By fully satisfying the guru with gifts, even one who knows the truth is freed from the bond of debt and thereby attains proper fitness for authority.

[tal-a28-v430] According to the Skandayamala, one who does not perform guru worship is born for a hundred lifetimes and only then becomes fit for authority and attains liberation.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a28-v431] Therefore a gift must certainly be given again to the guru: earlier it was declared as part of the rite, but this giving is for his satisfaction.

[tal-a28-v432] Then, having received his permission, the disciple may partake of what the guru has accepted; after that, he should worship the circle according to the resources available.

[tal-a28-v433] Without performing the teacher sacrifice, even completed rites remain undone; therefore the teacher sacrifice must be performed diligently according to one's strength.

[tal-a28-v434] Even if the teacher stays there, he is worshipful; having resolved as before, that substance should be used in the deity rite for devotees.

[tal-a28-v435] This rite is occasional, distinguished by parva, pavitra, and the rest.
